## Takeoff-file prices as a price source

Real takeoff exports often carry their own pricing columns; ingestion has always
stored them verbatim on `TakeoffLineItem.imported_material_unit_price` /
`imported_labor_hours_per_unit` (+ the two `*_factor` columns), but nothing
downstream ever read them — Stage 5 pricing is reference-only, so a number that never
becomes a price-book row is structurally invisible to it. Confirmed live on the
"Azul Plan 1" session (project `31da0d5a-...`): all three takeoff uploads carried
labor hours on every row and two carried material prices on every row, yet the agent
ran 120 price-book searches, asked the user 16 times, and 10 of the 14 material
prices the user hand-typed back exactly matched a price already sitting in their own
uploaded file. Closed by three additive pieces, none of which weaken the "the model
never retypes a number" guarantee:

- **`app/core/price_book/takeoff_promotion.py`** — the one door file numbers pass
  through into the price book. `promote_takeoff_prices` re-reads each current takeoff
  row's stored number server-side (the caller passes no figures, same posture as
  `set_estimate_prices`) and writes ordinary `source="imported"` `MaterialPrice` /
  `LaborProductivity` rows with `source_project_id` (+ `source_document_id` for
  materials) provenance — all pre-existing legal values/columns, **no migration**.
  Material identity resolves via the same `_find_or_create_material` path curation
  uses (label + resolved unit); labor hours become a `LaborActivity` named by the row
  label plus a productivity row. Rows with an unresolvable unit or zero/absent figure
  are skipped and reported, never guessed; the `*_factor` columns are recorded in the
  price row's notes but never applied (their semantics aren't knowable from the file
  — see `TakeoffLineItem`'s own docstring); re-promotion is idempotent (duplicate
  current price/productivity on the same identity → skipped). `add_material_price` /
  `add_productivity` gained optional `source`/provenance params (default `"manual"`,
  every pre-existing caller unchanged) rather than a second write path.
- **`get_estimate_pricing_state.takeoff_file_prices`** (`TakeoffFilePricesOut`,
  `app/core/estimates/pricing_state.py`) — present only when a current takeoff row
  carries a usable embedded figure: per-kind row counts, the carrying filenames, and
  per-kind `*_promoted` flags (existence of `source="imported"` rows with this
  project's `source_project_id`). Counting reuses the takeoff rows the state read
  already loads; only the two promoted-flag EXISTS queries are extra, and only when
  a file price exists at all. The MCP tool's summary message also nudges ("embedded
  prices not yet in the price book") so the model can't miss it.
- **The confirmation flow** — `promote_takeoff_prices` and `ask_user` were added to
  `PRICE_ESTIMATE_ALLOWED_TOOLS`, and the price directive gained step 2 (later steps
  renumbered 3-10, cross-references updated): when state shows unpromoted file
  prices, ask the user ONCE via `ask_user` (stable question key
  `use_takeoff_file_prices`, so `raise_setup_question`'s dedupe returns a prior
  answer instantly instead of re-asking — the "don't ask again after a decline"
  behavior is structural, not remembered), promote on a yes, proceed with the book
  alone on a no. The gate itself is prompt-level (like `record_user_supplied_price`'s
  only-what-the-user-typed rule); what's structural is that the tool takes no
  numbers. `ask_user` is scoped in the directive to this one question — ordinary
  missing-price questions still go through `create_pricing_request`.

**Verified**: full pytest suite green (1256 passed); `ruff` clean; live pass against a
throwaway Neon branch of the shared DB using the real Azul Plan 1 rows — see "How this
was verified" conventions (summary read → promotion → counts → idempotent rerun →
search finding the promoted prices). **Not verified**: a live LLM turn choosing to ask
and promote on its own judgment (same limitation as every other pass here), and the
`ask_user` question's frontend rendering in the pricing context.

**Deliberately not built**: automatic promotion at ingest (the user must confirm —
file prices can be stale bid-day numbers); a per-component "this row's file price"
hint on `ComponentPricingOut` (promotion makes ordinary search find them, which
covers the need without a second lookup path); applying the `*_factor` multipliers.

## Price book PDF ingestion

`docs/price-book.md` (§4) specified a CSV/XLSX-only, mapping-confirmed import flow for
materials/labor; PDF was out of scope there. This pass added PDF support for the
**materials** import (`POST /api/price-book/materials/preview` /
`.../materials/import` — no new routes) without touching a single line of the existing
CSV/XLSX code (`app/core/price_book/parsing.py::parse_table`). The only branch point is
`materials.py`'s `_load_table`: a `.pdf` filename routes to
`app/core/price_book/pdf_extraction.py::extract_pdf_price_table` instead of
`parse_table`; every downstream step (mapping, validation, `_import_one_row`, identity
resolution, unit resolution, duplicate detection) only ever sees the same `ParsedTable`/
`SourceRow` shape either path produces, and stays completely format-blind.

- **Two tiers, deterministic-first**, same precedent as takeoff's
  `column_mapping.py`/`table_layout.py`: `_extract_grid_table` (`pdfplumber`, a new
  dependency) reconstructs a real bordered table from actual text tokens and cell
  boundaries — same trust level as CSV/XLSX, no model involved. It abstains (`None`)
  on anything it isn't confident about (fewer than 2 named header columns, a duplicate
  normalized header, no rows at all) rather than guessing, since tier 2 is the safety
  net. `_extract_structured_llm` is that safety net: a Claude `messages.parse` call
  (`output_format=ExtractedPriceBookMaterials`) reads either the extracted text layer
  or, for a scanned PDF with none, native PDF vision (mirrors
  `app/core/vendor_bids/extraction.py`'s exact text-then-vision pattern), for a
  document with no grid to reconstruct at all (a repeating record/card layout, no
  ruling lines). Runs inline in the preview/import request cycle (not a background
  job, unlike vendor quote extraction), bounded at 90s.
- **The model both locates and transcribes in tier 2, unlike everywhere else in this
  pipeline** — a real, disclosed departure from "never let the model retype a
  number." Every row produced this way is still written immediately (so it's usable
  right away, same posture as vendor_bids' quote extraction), but its
  `price_book_import_rows` staging row is marked `resolution_status="ambiguous"`
  (already defined in the schema, previously unused by anything) with an explanatory
  note, rather than `"resolved"` like a trusted CSV/XLSX/pdf_grid row — both on the
  create path and on the duplicate-match path (a "this matches an existing price"
  determination rests on the same transcribed values a fresh row would; see "Verified
  live" below for the bug this caught). `preview`/`import` responses both carry a new
  `extraction_method` field (`null` | `"pdf_grid"` | `"pdf_llm"`) so a caller always
  knows which trust tier produced a given result without inspecting the file itself.
- **Closed real mapping-vocabulary gaps the sample files exposed, independent of
  PDF-ness** — a rich CSV/XLSX with the same columns would have hit them too.
  `TARGET_FIELDS`/`_HEADER_ALIASES` (`materials.py`) grew five fields: `csi_code`/
  `category` write onto `Material`'s existing (previously unmapped) columns;
  `priced_on` is now a per-row mappable date column, not just a whole-file override;
  `price_source`/`region`/`source_material_id` have no dedicated column and fold into
  `notes` instead of being silently dropped (`_compose_import_notes`).
  `price_source`'s `"vendor_quote"` value (case/spacing-insensitive) maps onto
  `MaterialPrice.source`'s real CHECK vocabulary; anything else (including a real but
  unlisted label like `"historical_avg"`) stays `"imported"`, never invented outside
  the CHECK — the raw label is preserved in `notes` either way
  (`_resolve_price_source`). `_find_or_create_material`'s bulk-import path gained the
  same fill-in-if-blank posture `create_material`'s manual-entry path already had for
  `csi_code`/`category`.
- **Not a new Anthropic-vs-OpenAI seam** — `price_book_pdf_extraction_model`
  defaults to `anthropic_model` and this is Claude-only, like takeoff column mapping
  and vendor quote extraction, not routed through `app/core/agent/provider.py`'s
  dual-provider abstraction (this is a pure ingestion-time concern, not agent-facing).
- **Identity/duplicate matching hardened against spacing and capitalization,
  format-agnostic (not a PDF-specific fix)** — every identity/duplicate lookup in
  `materials.py`/`labor.py`/`curation.py` compared a Python-side `key_text()`-normalized
  value (casefolded, internal whitespace collapsed) against a SQL-side
  `func.lower(func.trim(column))` — which only handles case and leading/trailing
  whitespace, not an internal run like `"Type  X  GWB"` (double space). New
  `app.core.price_book.parsing.normalized_text_column()` closes that gap
  (`func.regexp_replace(func.lower(func.trim(column)), r"\s+", " ", "g")`), applied
  everywhere: `Material.name`/`size_spec`/`manufacturer_part_number`/`manufacturer`,
  `VendorContact.company_name`, `MaterialPrice.vendor_name`, `LaborActivity.name`,
  `LaborClassification.trade`/`level`. Found one real, live bug in the process: labor
  import's `trade` parameter (a whole-file value, not a per-row column) was never run
  through any whitespace cleanup at all before comparison or storage — a stray leading/
  trailing space (an easy copy-paste accident) silently created a second, redundant
  `LaborClassification` instead of reusing the existing one. Fixed by normalizing
  `trade` once at `import_labor_price_file`'s entry (`clean_text(trade) or "General"`),
  the same "normalize once at the boundary" pattern used elsewhere in this codebase.
  Stored values always keep their original casing/punctuation (only the *comparison*
  is casefolded) — `key_text()`/`normalized_text_column()` are never used to decide
  what gets written, only what counts as "the same thing already exists."

## Audit/evidence design

- `agent_runs` / `tool_calls` / `evidence_refs` exist, but `agent_runs` is **not** created
  per MCP tool call — there's no protocol-level "conversation turn" boundary to hang it on.
  `tool_calls.run_id` is nullable and stays null for a bare tool call from a chat host; only
  a future whole-workflow REST endpoint (e.g. "price this project") would create one run and
  thread its id through.
- `run_logged_tool` (`app/core/audit.py`) is the only thing that writes `tool_calls`, and the
  only thing that commits *business-logic writes*. On success it commits the tool's writes +
  the success log together; on failure it rolls back the tool's writes and logs a separate
  failed row. Core service functions (`app/core/*/service.py`) must never call
  `session.commit()`. **One narrow, deliberate exception**: `set_current_tool` (also in
  `app/core/audit.py`, see "Live tool-call visibility" below) commits too, but only ever
  writes `agent_runs.current_tool_name`/`current_tool_started_at` — a live-progress marker,
  never `tool_calls` itself and never anything business-logic-bearing. `tool_calls` write
  exclusivity through `run_logged_tool` is unchanged.
- `evidence_refs` is populated **only** via the `evidence` argument callers pass to
  `write_priced_line` — a generic wrapper cannot know which historical row justified a price,
  only the caller that picked it knows that.

## Quote comparison spreadsheet

`app/core/spreadsheets/service.py` builds one of two DB-backed workbook modes, chosen
by one check: whether the project has any `takeoff_line_items` at all — nothing else
(quote count, import source) affects which mode is picked, and there is no mixed mode.
Projects with takeoff rows use `mode="takeoff"`: one row per takeoff line, vendor quote
columns, and estimator selection/adjustment columns that can be applied through
`POST .../apply-pricing`; only vendor quote lines matched to a takeoff line item appear
here; unmatched lines (including from a directly-uploaded quote document, even when the
project does have takeoff scope) are excluded from the grid but remain visible via
`list_vendor_quote_line_items`. Projects without takeoff rows use `mode="quote_material"`:
one stable row per persisted `QuoteMaterialGroup`, with vendor source lines assigned to
it regardless of takeoff match (there is none to match against). Quote-material mode is
comparison-only and rejects Apply Pricing because there is no takeoff scope. A project
with neither takeoff nor any uploaded quotes still resolves to `mode="quote_material"`,
just empty (`quote_count`/`row_count`/`vendor_count` all 0) rather than an error. Both
modes overlay estimator-owned JSON state from `project_spreadsheets`; canonical takeoff,
quote, and material-group rows remain protected source data.

Direct imports and RFQ responses share `QuoteSubmission` as the quote header. RFQ replies
use `source_kind="rfq_response"` and keep `rfq_id`; uploaded quote documents use
`source_kind="document_import"`, `rfq_id=NULL`, and `project_document_id`. Extracted rows
are stored in `vendor_quote_line_items`. The old `vendor_bid` document role, job name, MCP
names, and synthetic-RFQ data remain readable only as migration compatibility; new paths
normalize to `vendor_quote` and do not create synthetic RFQs.

## Vendor quote ingestion and grouping

`document_role=vendor_quote` uploads store the file and enqueue `vendor_quote.extract`.
The worker downloads the original, uses extracted text when available, and sends scanned
PDF page batches to Claude vision when text extraction is empty. Structured extraction
creates the `QuoteSubmission` and all `VendorQuoteLineItem` rows before grouping. Exact
duplicate rows from a single model response are removed; takeoff matching remains a
separate deterministic step used only when takeoff scope exists.

Each quote upload ensures one durable `quote_material.regroup` coordinator exists for the
project. The project-row lock serializes coordinator creation across simultaneous uploads.
The coordinator defers while any extraction is pending/running; deferral schedules the job
again without consuming an attempt or recording an error, then grouping runs as soon as
all extraction jobs are terminal. Failed documents do not block successfully extracted
quotes. Retry-import requeues failed extraction jobs and restores the coordinator.

Grouping loads all unprotected quote lines for the project, batches them through the
configured Claude grouping model, globally reconciles provisional groups, and persists
stable `QuoteMaterialGroup` identities where source-line overlap permits. One normalization
boundary repairs metadata-level model problems before strict validation: omitted known
lines become reviewable singletons, unapproved multi-line groups split into review
candidates, and malformed optional suggestions are dropped. Unknown source ids and
duplicate assignments remain hard failures. There is no fuzzy grouping fallback.

The material-group REST endpoints expose source lines and allow canonical edits, merges,
and moving/splitting lines. User corrections are authoritative: edited groups and groups
containing manually moved/merged lines are excluded from future automatic regrouping.
Import progress and failures are projected through both project overview and the quote
comparison artifact.

Below-threshold "these may be the same material" merge proposals are persisted as
`verification_requests` rows (kind `quote_group_merge`) rather than a bespoke suggestion
table — see "User verification queue" below. Each regroup supersedes the previous pending
proposals wholesale and raises fresh ones; user edits/merges/moves on a group supersede
pending proposals referencing it. The old `.../grouping-review-suggestions` endpoints
remain as thin compatibility wrappers over the same rows (same id namespace), so either
surface resolves the same request.

## User verification queue

One generic mechanism for "this output is too uncertain to stand without the user's
sign-off," shared by every pipeline stage and the chat agent — do not add another
bespoke review table/endpoint pair for a new stage; register a kind instead.

- **Envelope vs. meaning.** `verification_requests` (app/models/verification.py) holds
  only queue semantics: `kind`, `status` (`pending | resolved | dismissed | superseded`),
  `confidence`, `reason`, a polymorphic `subject_table`/`subject_id` pointer, a JSON
  `payload`, the user's `decision`, `raised_by` (`ingestion | grouping | agent`), a
  nullable `run_id` (threaded from `current_run_id` for agent-raised rows), and a
  `dedupe_key`. What a kind *means* lives in the registry
  (`app/core/verification/registry.py`), with one `VerificationKindSpec` per kind in
  `kinds.py`: payload schema (pydantic), allowed decisions, and a resolver that
  dispatches into the owning domain package. `kind`/`status` are plain strings validated
  by the registry, deliberately not Postgres enums.
- **Current kinds** (`app/core/verification/kinds.py`) — six registered: `quote_group_merge`
  (raised by grouping; resolver calls `material_groups.apply_group_merge_decision` —
  decisions `merge`/`keep_separate`); `takeoff_column_mapping` (raised by ingestion when
  the LLM header-mapping fallback ran; `accept` is a no-op confirm — a `remap` decision
  that re-parses is a deliberate follow-up, not implemented); `estimate_structure_issue`
  (raised by the estimates package for a low-confidence structural item/component;
  `confirm` sets `user_confirmed=True`, `exclude` writes an `EstimateSourceExclusion`);
  `quote_estimate_match` (raised when a quote line ambiguously matches more than one
  Estimate material component; `assign` sets
  `VendorQuoteLineItem.matched_estimate_component_id`, `leave_unmatched` clears it);
  `priced_line_proposal` (agent-raised via MCP, legacy pre-Estimate projects only;
  `accept` writes through `write_priced_line` with `source=user_input`); and
  `estimate_component_price_proposal` (agent-raised via MCP, the Estimate-domain analog
  — `accept` writes through `write_estimate_component_price` instead, since
  `priced_line_proposal` targets the wrong table once an Estimate exists). Only the last
  two are `agent_raisable`; the other four are pipeline-raised only. `dismiss` is
  universal on every kind and never runs a resolver.
- **One REST surface** (`app/api/verifications.py`): list + resolve. Decisions are
  enumerated in the response so a frontend can render unknown kinds generically.
  Pending counts per kind are projected into `GET /overview`.
- **Convergence rule — supersede on authoritative write.** Any authoritative write to a
  subject supersedes its pending requests: `write_priced_line`/
  `write_estimate_component_price` supersede pending proposals for that subject (so chat
  re-prices, spreadsheet apply-pricing, and the accept-resolver itself all clear stale
  proposals by construction); group edits/merges/moves supersede pending
  `quote_group_merge`s that reference the touched groups; producers re-raising the same
  finding supersede via `dedupe_key`. Nothing pends forever against reality, and nothing
  blocks on a pending request — they are advisory, not locks.
- **Import-order note:** domain modules import `verification.service` at module level,
  while `kinds.py` is imported lazily by the service on first use
  (`ensure_kinds_registered`) precisely so its resolvers can reference those same domain
  modules. Anything touching the registry *before* a service call (e.g. the MCP tool)
  must call `ensure_kinds_registered()` first.

## Takeoff column mapping (LLM fallback)

Real takeoff files arrive with arbitrary column headers (`"What estimator wrote"`,
`"Counted amount"`, `"Measure-ish"`, etc.) that a fixed alias list will never fully
cover, sometimes with no single clean header row at all (a logo/title block, a header
split across two physical rows, several distinct tables in one sheet), and sometimes
with a column-name choice that's structurally *wrong* rather than the data itself
being bad. Despite the section title, this now covers all of takeoff-file parsing, not
just column-name mapping — four layered mechanisms, each opt-in and best-effort (any
LLM failure degrades to whatever the prior layer already produced, never raises):

1. **Format support.** `app/core/ingestion/parsers.py`'s `parse_takeoff_file` (async)
   handles CSV, XLSX (`openpyxl`), and legacy binary XLS (`xlrd` — `openpyxl` only
   reads `.xlsx`/`.xlsm`; `.xls` is still common from older estimating-tool exports).
   `_xls_rows` and `_xlsx_rows` both funnel into the same `_rows_from_worksheet_values`,
   so every mechanism below applies identically regardless of which container format
   the file arrived in — only the raw-grid extraction differs.
   `app/core/ingestion/service.py`'s `_is_supported_takeoff_file`/
   `normalize_document_role` accept `.xls` the same way as `.xlsx`. PDF takeoffs remain
   unsupported — a deliberately deferred scope decision, not an oversight.
2. **Deterministic header-row detection, multi-block-aware.** `_find_header_rows`
   (plural) scans the *whole* sheet, not just an initial window, for every row
   matching a real takeoff header signature (a quantity header alongside a
   label/description header), and `_rows_from_worksheet_values` gives each occurrence
   its own independent header→column mapping and data span. This exists because real
   exports sometimes repeat the exact same title+header block multiple times down one
   sheet (one printed "page" per phase) — treating only the first occurrence as
   authoritative silently dropped every later block. Falls back to a loose "≥2 filled
   cells in the first 10 rows" heuristic, once, only when no strict signature is found
   anywhere in the sheet.
3. **Column-mapping LLM fallback (tier 1).**
   `app/core/ingestion/column_mapping.py`'s `maybe_map_columns_with_llm`, gated by
   `TAKEOFF_COLUMN_MAPPING_MODE` (currently `llm_fallback` in `.env`; code default is
   `deterministic` | `llm_fallback` | `llm_always`, same shape as
   `document_query_expansion_mode`). In `llm_fallback` mode it's only invoked when the
   header row itself can't resolve label/quantity/unit deterministically (checked once
   at the header level, not per row). Uses `takeoff_column_mapping_model`
   (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`), a separate setting from `anthropic_model` — a small
   classification-style call (headers + a few sample rows in, a header-to-schema-field
   mapping out). It never transcribes a cell value itself — row values are still parsed
   by the existing deterministic code (`_parse_quantity`, subtotal rejection, etc.)
   against whichever header the mapping points at, so a confidently-wrong mapping
   produces skipped rows, never silently-wrong data, by construction.
   - **Two deterministic guards run on whatever mapping the LLM returns, before it's
     ever accepted** — both added after live (non-mocked) testing against two real
     files (`temp-test-files/Oro Takeoff.xlsx`, `Azul Takeoff.xls`) surfaced the model
     making a plausible-but-wrong column choice, even when the *correct* column was
     identified elsewhere in the very same response:
     - `_guard_against_fragment_label` — swaps `label`↔`description` when `label`'s
       chosen column's sample values are, on average, at least 2x shorter *and* at
       least 6 characters shorter than `description`'s. Confirmed live case: the model
       mapped `label` to a "Size" column (`'3"'`, `'7504W'`) while correctly
       identifying a separate "Description" column holding the real item names in the
       same response, producing labels like `'3"'` instead of `'3" HOCKEY STICK'`.
     - `_guard_against_extended_total_rate` — rejects a `material_unit_price`/
       `labor_hours_per_unit` mapping whose *own header text* contains a rollup token
       (`result`/`total`/`extended`/`subtotal`/`amount`/`sum`), swapping to an unused
       header containing `"unit"` if one exists, else nulling the field outright.
       Confirmed live case: the model mapped `material_unit_price` to a "Material
       Result" column (= unit price × quantity) — invisible on quantity=1 rows, but
       silently 2x wrong on a quantity=2 row (`$16` unit price imported as `$32`).
       Nulling when no replacement candidate exists is deliberate: a missing price is
       far safer than a wrong one silently feeding pricing math later.
     Both guards are pure functions with dedicated tests (`tests/test_column_mapping.py`).
     Both prompt sections were also strengthened to explicitly warn against the exact
     failure pattern observed, as a cheap complement to the hard guard — not a
     replacement for it, since the guard is what still catches a future regression on
     a model call the prompt fix doesn't prevent.
4. **Table-layout LLM fallback (tier 2), a further fallback beyond tier 1.**
   `app/core/ingestion/table_layout.py`'s `maybe_locate_tables_with_llm`, gated by
   `takeoff_table_layout_mode` (`.env`/code default `deterministic`, i.e. off). Only
   consulted when tier 1 (deterministic scanning plus column mapping together) still
   produces zero usable rows for a worksheet, *or* a suspiciously high skip ratio
   (`_should_try_table_layout`, gated by `takeoff_table_layout_skip_ratio_threshold`,
   default `0.5` — deliberately conservative, well above a normal messy real file's
   ~25% skip rate, and only applied once a worksheet has enough nonblank rows for a
   ratio to mean anything). Unlike tier 1, this is handed the raw, un-sliced worksheet
   grid (logo/title block and all) and returns only structural coordinates — header row
   range(s), a data row range, and a column *index* (never a header string, since a
   multi-row or missing header may have no reliable text to key off at all) for each
   schema field — never a transcribed value; `parsers.py`'s existing value-parsing code
   still owns every number, mirroring tier 1's safety invariant one level up. Uses
   `takeoff_table_layout_model` (defaults to `anthropic_model`, not the cheap one —
   locating a table amid noise is a harder structural-reasoning task than tier 1's
   "map this one already-clean header row"). `_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=180`/
   `_MAX_GRID_ROWS=2000`/`_MAX_GRID_COLS=60`/`_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8000` were widened from
   initially conservative defaults after a real 425-row/33-column/6-table paginated
   export needed all of that headroom and over 60s of reasoning to locate every block —
   this fallback only ever runs inside an async ingestion job, never a live request, so
   the wider budget costs nothing user-facing. No `temperature` param is passed to the
   API call — newer Claude models (e.g. `claude-sonnet-5`, this setting's default)
   reject it outright with a 400 that the caller's best-effort exception handling was
   silently swallowing as "the LLM found nothing," which masked this fallback failing
   on every single call regardless of grid size until traced down directly.
5. **Assembly propagation from unitless header rows.** Real takeoff exports often
   interleave category/subgroup header rows directly in the row stream instead of
   using a dedicated assembly/category column — e.g. a zero-quantity divider row like
   `"UNDERGROUND"`, then a nested `"LENNAR 200A"` title row, then the real, unit-bearing
   line items belonging to it. These rows fail the ordinary quantity/unit checks and
   used to be silently dropped with no trace. `parse_takeoff_file`'s main loop now
   tracks a running "current group label" while walking rows in order: a skipped row
   updates it only when it has **no unit at all** but does carry real label/description
   text (`_group_header_text`) — the one reliable signal distinguishing an
   organizational divider from a real line item, since even a genuine zero-quantity
   catalog item still carries a real unit and correctly leaves the context untouched.
   Every real parsed row that doesn't already have its own `assembly` (from a dedicated
   column, when one exists) gets stamped with the most recently seen group label.
   Confirmed live against Azul Takeoff.xls: all 138 real rows now carry the correct
   nested group label matching the file's own structure, where previously `assembly`
   was null for all of them. **Only wired into the main deterministic/column-mapping
   path so far** — the table-layout fallback's separate row-extraction code
   (`_rows_from_table_region`) doesn't get this treatment yet, since neither real file
   tested this session ever needed tier 2 to engage.
- Any LLM failure at either tier (no API key, timeout, malformed JSON, rejected
  request) makes the corresponding `maybe_*` function return `None` rather than raise —
  the caller keeps whatever the prior layer already produced.
- When either LLM tier *was* used, ingestion raises a verification request so the user
  can confirm the parse before it's trusted (see "User verification queue" above) —
  `takeoff_column_mapping` (tier 1, carrying the chosen mapping/headers/parsed-skipped
  counts) or `takeoff_table_layout` (tier 2, carrying the located region(s) per sheet).
  Both are accept-only today (no `remap`/`reclassify` resolver yet, matching the
  existing deferred-follow-up pattern elsewhere in this queue) — the upload itself is
  never blocked on either.

**Not verified against a live Postgres this pass** — `.xls` support, both
column-mapping guards, and the assembly-propagation fix were all verified via
`ruff check .`, the full test suite, and live (non-mocked) Anthropic API calls against
two real files, but not re-run through the full ingest→job-handler→DB-write path this
session. That full path *was* exercised once, manually, against the live shared Neon
DB for the Oro file (see "How this was verified" below) — but before these fixes

## File storage (Cloudflare R2)

R2 speaks the S3 API directly, so `app/core/storage/blob.py` talks to it with
`aioboto3` (`endpoint_url=R2_ENDPOINT_URL`, `region_name="auto"`,
`Config(signature_version="s3v4")`) — no subprocess sidecar needed, unlike the earlier
Vercel Blob integration this replaced. Credentials come from `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`/
`R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`/`R2_BUCKET_NAME`/`R2_ENDPOINT_URL`. The bucket
has **no public base URL** configured (no custom domain, no r2.dev binding), so nothing
is ever stored as a permanently public link: `upload_document` returns the object's
storage key, and `ProjectDocument.blob_url` persists that key (the column name predates
the switch and now holds a key, not a URL). Reads never persist a presigned URL — every
caller that needs a fetchable link mints one fresh, on demand, via `get_presigned_url`
(default 1-hour expiry): `app/core/project/document_catalog.py`'s `list_project_documents` and
`app/api/documents.py`'s upload response both call it directly at the point they return
a link to the frontend, rather than presigning once and storing the result. Server-side
re-reads that never leave the backend (e.g. the `vendor_quote.extract` job) skip
presigning entirely and call `download_document`, which fetches bytes straight from R2
via an authenticated `get_object`.

### The web/worker document-queue split, and how it's enforced

`app/config.py`'s `_cross_field_runtime_bounds` validator hard-fails startup whenever
`RENDER=true` (which Render injects automatically) unless: `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT=
production`, `DOCUMENT_EXTRACTOR=native`, `WEB_CONCURRENCY=1`, every R2/DB/Voyage
secret is present and non-localhost, and **exactly one** of `DOCUMENT_WORKERS_ENABLED`
/ `DOCUMENT_WORKERS_DELEGATED` is `true` — the validator explicitly rejects both `true`
(ambiguous — in-process queues and a separate worker service both trying to own the
same queues) and both `false` (nobody would be running the document queues at all).
This is a real, code-level guarantee, not just a convention documented here — a
misconfigured Render service refuses to boot rather than silently double-processing or
dropping document jobs.

- **Web service env**: `DOCUMENT_WORKERS_ENABLED=false`, `DOCUMENT_WORKERS_DELEGATED=
  true`, `JOBS_WORKER_ENABLED=true`. The web process does *not* run the document
  queues in-process, but still runs every *other* job queue in-process (RFQ send, quote
  regroup, etc.) via its own `JOBS_WORKER_ENABLED` flag — the split is document-queue-
  specific, not "web never runs jobs."
- **Worker service env**: `DOCUMENT_WORKERS_ENABLED=true` (and no `JOBS_WORKER_ENABLED`
  — it only runs the three document queues via `app.workers.document_queues`, nothing
  else).
- Anyone changing one service's worker-split flags must know the other's — they're a
  matched pair, not independently tunable. Both services also set `DOCUMENT_PIPELINE_
  VERSION=document-foundation-v3` identically; letting these drift between the two
  processes would be a real, hard-to-diagnose ingestion bug.
- `maxShutdownDelaySeconds: 300` on both services is not an arbitrary number — it's
  what makes room for the already-documented "Queue control-plane isolation and
  cancellation" behavior below: deploy shutdown drains in-flight work, then releases
  still-owned leases without consuming a retry attempt, rather than hard-killing the
  process mid-lease.

# Agent Instructions

Refer to `CLAUDE.md` for the project instructions and conventions before making changes in this repository.

## Document and ingestion UX

- Create enters the Agent workspace immediately; project saving, uploads and processing continue in the account-scoped background coordinator.
- Keep file/folder selection, navigation and reading available during active work. Append overlapping submissions under one bounded concurrency budget.
- Preserve local originals, account/project-scoped caches and unsaved review drafts across route changes. Clear sensitive caches on logout/account change.

- Needs Review requires a specific unresolved review request, an understandable reason and a working action. Provider/configuration failures are operational recovery issues, not content reviews.
- Retry transient failures with bounded, duplicate-safe recovery. Preserve successful stages and originals; show compact truthful intervention after recovery is exhausted. Never fabricate success or conceal unsaved data.
- Status labels must remain readable with the sidebar open and on mobile. Readers support reachable horizontal/vertical scrolling and fullscreen without making fullscreen mandatory.

- Amend the existing linked PRs and retain source provenance. Start with a short, plain-English before/after summary of each changed feature.
- Use neutral project names and task-based headings, not dated checkpoint headings or personal test-project names.

- Keep exact timestamps, environment identities and private test-project IDs in the evidence ledger where needed for reproducibility; never expose credentials.

# Rialto Frontend

## Current development rules

Read `AGENTS.md` and both actual checkout CLAUDE files before cross-repository work.
Its mandatory context, resource safety, retention and reviewer-delivery rules apply.
`docs/STANDARDS_AUDIT.md` separates verified behavior from unresolved compliance.
Tests passing is not evidence that every subsystem already meets every rule below.

## Coding agent instructions

Any coding agent working in this repo should use the **graphify** skill/tool
(`/graphify`) to build and query a knowledge graph of the codebase before doing
broad exploration, architecture questions, or cross-file consistency analysis —
prefer it over ad hoc grepping when the question is about how the codebase or its
files relate to each other. If `graphify-out/` already exists, treat that as the
graph to query first.

## Product

Rialto automates pricing/estimating for construction subcontractors. A sub uploads a
takeoff (spreadsheet of line items) plus spec/addenda files; a backend pricing agent
prices every line item — checking historical pricing, checking spec context, falling
back to web-search-informed reasoning, and (only on explicit user request) drafting RFQs
to vendors. Every price carries a `source` (historical match / agent estimate / RFQ quote
/ user input) and a confidence score. This repo is the UI a sub actually uses to drive
that flow.

## What this repo is — and is not

- This is the product frontend only. It renders data and calls the backend's REST API —
  nothing more.
- **No pricing, matching, or RFQ logic lives here.** All of that is `rialto-backend`'s
  job (its own business logic layer, and an MCP-tool-driven pricing agent).
- **Never talks to Postgres or any datastore directly.** Every piece of data comes from
  `rialto-backend` over its REST API.
- **Never parse chat prose to extract structured data.** The agent chat endpoint returns
  ordered content blocks for display and plain text only as prose/fallback. If a screen
  needs a price, a status, or an RFQ id, it comes from a structured REST endpoint or an
  artifact block provided by the backend — not from scraping the chat reply. If no such
  endpoint exists yet, the screen is blocked, not worked around; see `CONTRACT.md`.
- Backend repo lives at `../rialto-backend` (sibling directory). Its own `CLAUDE.md`
  documents its architecture rules, MCP tool catalog, and open follow-ups in detail —
  read it before assuming a data shape.

## The API contract

**`CONTRACT.md` is the source of truth for every endpoint this frontend calls** —
paths, methods, request/response schemas, enums, and (critically) which pieces of backend
functionality are real REST endpoints vs. MCP-tool-only (not callable by this frontend at
all yet). Before building or modifying a screen:

1. Check `CONTRACT.md` for the endpoint(s) it needs.
2. If the endpoint exists, use its documented shape exactly — don't hand-write a type
   from memory or guess a field name.
3. If the endpoint doesn't exist yet (marked ⚠️ MCP-tool-only or ❌ not implemented), the
   screen is blocked — flag it, don't build a workaround (e.g. don't reconstruct a
   pricing table by parsing chat replies).
4. If you discover the contract is stale (a field renamed, a new endpoint added on the
   backend), update `CONTRACT.md` itself first, then the frontend code.

The backend now requires authentication on every REST endpoint (per-user accounts, enforced
via Postgres RLS on `rialto-backend`'s side). Login/refresh/logout are documented in
`CONTRACT.md`. `apiFetch` (`src/lib/api-client.ts`) attaches the bearer token and handles
401 → refresh → retry automatically — call sites don't need to think about auth at all.
There is still no self-registration; accounts are provisioned by whoever owns
`rialto-backend`.

## Tech stack

- **Vite + React** (TypeScript) — SPA, no server runtime. Chosen over Next.js because
  there's no SEO need and auth is handled entirely client-side (bearer token in memory,
  refresh via an httpOnly cookie the backend owns); revisit only if server-side secrets
  become necessary.
- **Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui** — component source is copied into this repo (not an opaque
  dependency), fits a table/form/dialog-heavy dashboard (pricing table, RFQ forms,
  document viewer).
- **TanStack Query** for all data fetching — server state (projects, chat history,
  whatever structured views exist) goes through it; don't hand-roll fetch+useState for
  anything that hits the backend.
- **pnpm** as the package manager.
- Greenfield — no existing design system/brand to match.

## Architecture rule: dashboards and chat are decoupled

Sending a chat message may cause backend side effects (a price written, an RFQ created).
The frontend's response to that is to invalidate/refetch the relevant structured
TanStack Query, not to parse the reply text for what changed. Chat is a conversation
view that renders backend-authored `content_blocks`; dashboards are structured-data
views backed by their own endpoints. Don't blend the two by extracting data from prose.

## Repo structure

```
src/
  api/           Thin fetch wrappers, one file per CONTRACT.md resource
                 (projects.ts, documents.ts, agentMessages.ts). No logic beyond
                 building the request and typing the response.
  queries/       TanStack Query hooks (useProjects, useProject, useCreateProject,
                 useUploadDocument, useAgentMessages, useSendAgentMessage).
  types/         contract.ts -- types mirrored from CONTRACT.md. Edit the contract
                 first if a shape needs to change, then this file, never the reverse.
  components/
    ui/          shadcn/ui generated components -- regenerate via `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest
                 add <name>`, don't hand-edit generated primitives beyond what shadcn
                 itself lets you customize at generation time.
    layout/      AppShell.tsx (sidebar + <Outlet/>), Sidebar.tsx (persistent nav +
                 project tree).
    ProjectCreateDialog.tsx, DocumentUpload.tsx, ChatThread.tsx
  routes/        ProjectListPage.tsx, ProjectDetailLayout.tsx (tabs + rail + <Outlet/>),
                 ProjectOverviewPage.tsx, ProjectChatPage.tsx, ProjectDocumentsPage.tsx,
                 ContactsPage.tsx -- one file per route, wired up in App.tsx.
  lib/           api-client.ts (fetch wrapper + ApiError), query-client.ts, utils.ts (shadcn cn()).
  App.tsx        QueryClientProvider + BrowserRouter + nested route table.
```

Current routes:
- `/` -- project list + create (real).
- `/projects/:projectId` -- redirects to `overview`.
- `/projects/:projectId/overview` -- DB-backed project dashboard summary using

- `/projects/:projectId/chat` -- the real chat thread.
- `/projects/:projectId/documents` -- direct browser-to-R2 multipart upload plus the

- `/admin` -- hidden internal operator console (create accounts, list all accounts,

- `/contacts` -- table shell, genuine empty state (`list_vendor_contacts` is MCP-only, and

## Design reference (2026-07-05)

The visual design (sidebar nav + project tree, right-hand project rail, stage tracker,
card-based dashboard, warm cream/orange palette) was modeled on a design pass through
`UseRialto/rialto-ai-for-estimating` (the `rfq-agent-refactor` branch, the most complete
recent UI at the time) -- **cloned temporarily, run locally, screenshotted, then deleted**.
Only the visual look and screen/interaction intent were used; no code, logic, or
architecture was ported, and none should be in future passes either -- if that repo is
consulted again, treat it the same way (temporary clone, visual reference only, delete
when done).

Two categories of "not real yet" content came out of that pass, and they're handled
differently -- keep this distinction when adding to either:

1. **Backend capability exists (MCP tool or model), just not REST-exposed** -- e.g. pricing
   status writers. These render a genuine, honest empty state ("not available via the API
   yet") -- never fabricated rows.
2. **No backend concept exists anywhere** -- e.g. the 5-step stage tracker, the project
   rail's GC/due-date/estimated-size/project-owner fields, and the "Mode" role selector.
   These were built as
   **static chrome** matching the reference's visual shape (per explicit instruction) --
   neutral placeholders (`—`, "Not available yet"), never per-project fabricated values.
   If a real concept for any of these gets added to the backend, wire it up for real and
   drop the "chrome" framing -- don't leave it static once there's something to bind to.

**Talking to the backend in local dev**: `vite.config.ts` proxies API requests to
`BACKEND_DEV_URL` (environment override; default `http://localhost:8000`). An empty
`VITE_API_BASE_URL` uses relative same-origin URLs. The Python backend already
supports CORS through `settings.cors_allowed_origins` in `app/main.py`; inspect the
isolated target's actual configuration rather than assuming CORS is absent. Never
put backend or storage credentials into frontend environment variables.

The proxy only exists in `vite dev` -- `pnpm preview` and any real deployment serve static
files with no proxy, so `VITE_API_BASE_URL` must be a real URL and the backend needs real
CORS in those contexts. Don't debug a "works in dev, breaks in preview/prod" API call as
if it's an app bug -- it's this proxy not existing outside the dev server.

Document part uploads are the exception to the API proxy: the backend returns short-lived
presigned R2 URLs and the browser sends each part directly to the private bucket. The R2

## Product

Rialto helps construction subcontractors build estimates from original documents,
takeoff quantities, and traceable price evidence. Preserve source quantities,
prices, units, locations and citations. Never invent a price to complete an estimate.
Use price-book references or explicit user-supplied inputs; reusable price-book
promotion requires explicit intent. Draft/send RFQs only on explicit user request;
sending is queued and requires the applicable approval. Uploading documents does
not require Identify Scope or block chat and original-file reading.

- `POST /api/projects` creates a name-only shell. Documents upload independently and
  concurrently through browser-to-R2 multipart initiation/part/complete/abort routes.
  A source upload is immutable and content-addressed by SHA-256 within its project.
- `ProjectDocument` is one uploaded revision. `DocumentProcessingRun` is an immutable
  extraction/index version. Pages, nodes, entities, and takeoff materializations belong
  to a run; its complete structured/lexical foundation becomes current atomically, then
  only embedding/capability fields are checkpointed onto that same run. A failed
  reprocessing attempt never removes the last searchable version or breaks citations.
- `document.prepare` is role-routed to separately supervised `document_structured` or
  `document_native` queues. It verifies bytes/MIME, reuses warm Docling converters,
  applies bounded selective OCR, renders page images, uploads page assets concurrently,
  preserves tables/coordinates, and publishes lexical evidence first. Independent
  `document.enrich.text` and `document.enrich.visual` jobs run concurrently on
  `document_enrichment`, checkpoint every successful batch, and fan into
  `document.enrich.finalize`. Text enrichment covers every node; visual enrichment
  covers all drawing sheets but only visually ambiguous/table/image-heavy spec pages.
  Voyage calls reserve from a shared Postgres-backed per-model rate budget.
- Lexical evidence may remain available while enrichment is processing or needs review.
  Canonical project setup and scope summaries are different: they require every active
  document's role-specific enrichment and are keyed to an immutable source-snapshot hash.
  A degraded lexical index must never produce durable project understanding silently.
- Exact construction identifiers remain first-class. Retrieval batches up to 12 typed
  questions and combines deterministic entity lookup, capability-selected PostgreSQL
  FTS or Lakebase BM25, Voyage dense text, and optional visual-page candidates with
  weighted reciprocal-rank fusion, sibling diversity, and a bounded Voyage reranker.
  Portable GIN/HNSW is the deployment baseline; Lakebase BM25/ANN is the explicit
  post-ingestion production accelerator described in `docs/lakebase-search.md`. Do not
  replace this with dense-only search or an agent-driven chain of low-level search/read
  calls.
- The normal agent surface is `list_project_documents`, `retrieve_project_evidence`,
  `get_document_context`, and `inspect_document_page`. The last tool performs targeted
  Anthropic vision only after retrieval selects a page and persists the result as a
  non-verbatim observation node. **Correction: `get_document_outline` is not part of
  this surface** — confirmed dead (not registered as an MCP tool, no service function,
  no REST route; see "Live MCP tool registry (authoritative)" below). Nothing currently
  replaces whole-document table-of-contents browsing — `get_document_context` only
  expands an already-cited node's immediate neighborhood, and `list_project_documents`
  is inventory-only (filename/role/status, no section structure). This is a real,
  disclosed capability gap, not a renamed tool.
- `DocumentNode.source_text` is citable source evidence. `contextual_prefix` is
  separately labeled retrieval context and must never be quoted as source text. Evidence
  writes accept stable `document_nodes` UUID pointers and validate project/current-run
  ownership.
- `supersedes` retires the target revision; `amends` leaves the base active and controls
  only its declared scope. Revision dates never establish precedence or alter relevance
  ranking. Retrieval exposes relation/conflict metadata so the agent cites both sides
  when amendment scope is ambiguous.
- `document_pages` may carry a 1024-dimensional `voyage-multimodal-3.5` vector;
  `document_nodes` use 1024-dimensional `voyage-context-4`; final reranking uses
  `rerank-2.5`. Provider failures degrade to lexical retrieval, while database/index
  errors fail closed.
- Retrieval changes require the reviewed golden-set process in
  `docs/retrieval-evaluation.md`. Unit tests alone do not establish retrieval quality.

The retired document paths have no backward-compatibility promise. Do not add v2

## Estimating domain model: Assembly, Estimate Item, Cost Component

The CSI Estimate workflow (`app/core/estimates/`, tools covered in "MCP tool catalog"
below) mirrors how a human estimator actually builds a bid — not a flat list of priced
takeoff rows. Three concepts, smallest to largest:

- **Cost Component** (`EstimateCostComponent`, `app/models/estimate.py`) — the true
  atom. `cost_type` is one of `material | labor | equipment | subcontract | other`: a
  quantity, a unit, a rate, nothing more. A component can never stand alone on a bid —
  "500 SF of gypsum board" or "40 labor-hours" means nothing without the installed work
  it belongs to. `scope` is `direct` (nested under one `estimate_item_id`) or `project`
  (a project-wide cost with no `estimate_item_id`, written only via `write_project_cost`).
- **Estimate Item** (`EstimateItem`) — the smallest thing that IS a sellable, priceable
  unit of real installed work: one CSI-coded crew task ("Hang and finish 5/8" GWB, Wall
  Type A, 2nd floor corridor"), never a bare material, bare labor hours, or a category
  header. It carries `csi_code`/`csi_title`/`quantity`/`unit` and rolls up its nested
  Cost Components' prices into a total — it never gets its own separate price. This is
  the unit `propose_estimate_structure` writes and `get_estimate_structure` reads back.
- **Assembly** — a named system grouping several Estimate Items together (e.g. "Wall
  Type A" = framing + board + finish + insulation), for the estimator's mental model
  only — its total is just the sum of its Estimate Items, it's never priced directly,
  within the `EstimateItem`/`EstimateCostComponent` graph itself: `EstimateItem` has no
  `assembly` column, and nothing groups multiple `EstimateItem` rows by a shared
  assembly identity inside `app/core/estimates/`. The only `assembly` field inside that
  graph is a free-text string on `TakeoffLineItem`, populated from the takeoff CSV's
  `assembly`/`category`/`system`/`wall_type` column (`app/core/ingestion/parsers.py`'s
  `_ASSEMBLY_HEADERS`) and surfaced read-only via `EstimateSourceRowOut` for context —
  treat *that* as a reasoning aid, not a queryable grouping.

  **Correction — a real Assembly recipe library now exists as a separate system,
  contradicting older language in this section that called Assembly "not a first-class
  entity" without qualification.** `app/models/assembly.py` (`Assembly` →
  `AssemblyVersion` → `AssemblyVersionItem` → `AssemblyVersionComponent`, mirroring the
  same mutable-identity/immutable-published-version split as price-book Material) plus
  full CRUD/publish/retire/component-mutation service (`app/core/assemblies/service.py`)
  and REST API (`app/api/assemblies.py`: `POST/GET/PATCH /api/assemblies`, `.../versions`,
  `.../versions/{id}/publish`, `.../versions/{id}/retire`, `.../versions/{id}/components`,
  plus hybrid ILIKE+`pg_trgm` search via `GET /api/assemblies?q=`) are implemented and
  documented in full in `docs/assemblies.md`, whose own header states status:
  "implemented and verified on the Neon dev branch `pricebook-dev`... not yet migrated
  to production, no MCP tools yet." So as of this pass: **creation, publishing, and
  searching are built**; only **recipe expansion is still genuinely unbuilt** — nothing
  in `app/core/assemblies/` applies/instantiates a published `AssemblyVersion` into
  actual `EstimateItem`/`EstimateCostComponent` rows, and it isn't wired into any
  MCP tool yet, so the chat agent cannot use it. `app/models/estimate.py`'s
  `estimate_version_assembly_instances` table already reserves a lineage FK toward this
  system for when that expansion step lands. **Also unresolved, not verified this
  pass**: `Assembly`/`AssemblyVersion` carry a nullable `org_id` but no `user_id` column
  at all — unclear whether this is deliberate (a shared, company-wide recipe library,
  the same posture price-book `Material` had before the `3698854` cross-tenant leak fix

Hierarchy:
```
Assembly ("Wall Type A")                    -- grouping label, never priced itself
 └─ Estimate Item ("Hang 5/8" GWB, Wall A")  -- the atomic sellable unit, ONE price
     ├─ Cost Component: material  (cost_type=material)
     ├─ Cost Component: labor     (cost_type=labor)
     └─ Cost Component: equipment/subcontract/other, if needed
```

### Additive V2 estimate core

`app/core/estimates/` and `app/models/estimate.py` contain a backend-only V2
foundation built alongside V1. Existing projects default to `estimate_schema_version=1`
and are never migrated implicitly. V2 exposes immutable whole-estimate versions as the
business concept, but persists each version as a complete lightweight manifest over
project-scoped logical identities and copy-on-write item/component revisions. Unchanged
revisions are shared across commits and cloned scenarios. V2 also provides relational
locations/dimensions, joint allocation slices, explicit labor bases, selected pricing
calculations, waste state, typed changesets, and metric-grain reporting. Units are
**not** a V2-owned concept: `estimate_v2.py` used to define its own `Unit`/`UnitAlias`
mapped to the `units` table, which collided with price-book's own `Unit`/`UnitAlias`
(`app/models/units.py`, the live, callers-having version) also mapped to that same
table — that duplicate mapping broke `app.main` import outright. V2 now imports
price-book's `Unit` directly (`app/core/estimates/calculations.py`'s
`convert_quantity`, `.../service.py`'s unit resolution, both via
`app.core.price_book.units.resolve_unit`) rather than owning a parallel controlled-unit
system. There are intentionally no V2 REST routes, MCP tools, agent workflows, price-book
adapters, frontend consumers, or existing-project backfill.

**How an Estimate Item actually gets derived** — the reasoning `propose_estimate_structure`
expects before it's called, one takeoff row at a time, three questions in order:

1. **Where is this?** Locate the takeoff quantity on the drawings — which wall, room,
   floor — using one batched `retrieve_project_evidence` request, then
   `inspect_document_page` for a verified, page-level read only when indexed evidence is
   insufficient. This is what tells you the assembly/wall-type context.
2. **What does it require?** Retrieve the spec evidence and a bounded structural window
   (`retrieve_project_evidence` then `get_document_context`) — layers, fire rating,
   finish level — to determine
   which real work activities are actually needed (framing? one layer or two? a finish
   coat?).
3. **Is this a real, standalone piece of installed work?** If the takeoff row plus
   drawing location plus spec requirement together describe one crew-doable task with a
   confirmed quantity, it becomes an Estimate Item (`origin=imported_qto` or `inferred`,
   `quantity_status=exact`/`derived`). If the location or requirement can't be confirmed,
   it does **not** get guessed into an Estimate Item — `propose_estimate_structure`'s own
   docstring says to "leave unsupported rows unmapped for review": an unresolved source
   row, never a fabricated one. A row left this way can be left implicitly unmapped, or
   explicitly declared via `EstimateDraftIn.unresolved_source_rows`
   (`EstimateSourceUnresolvedIn`, `app/core/estimates/types.py`) — a `takeoff_line_item_id`
   plus a required `reason` string. Either way the row surfaces as an `unassigned_source_row`
   verification issue (`issue_type="unassigned_source_row"`, see "User verification queue"),
   but an explicit `unresolved_source_rows` entry replaces that issue's generic fallback
   text ("This imported takeoff row is not assigned...") with the agent's own stated reason
   — the more useful signal for whoever triages that queue.

**A takeoff row's quantity does not have to go entirely to one Estimate Item.** The same
material can serve different work in different locations (500 SF of board: 300 SF to
Wall Type A, 150 to Wall Type B, 50 to Wall Type C) — `EstimateSourceMappingIn.quantity`
(`app/core/estimates/types.py`) lets a `row_type=material` mapping claim a portion of the
source row rather than always the full amount (omit it to consume the row's full
quantity, backward compatible). The quantities mapped to one source row across a whole
proposal can never sum to more than that row's total quantity — over-allocation rejects
the entire proposal (`app/core/estimates/service.py::_expand_source_row_mappings`). Only
`material` mappings carry this quantity semantic; `installed_work`/`allowance` mappings
still cannot repeat the same source row within one proposal, since there's no split
rationale for them. The raw `source_takeoff_line_item_ids` list field (as opposed to
`source_row_mappings`) remains a quantity-blind, unenforced loophole — multiple
items/components can still reference the same row through it with no accounting; that's
accepted, not fixed.

**`quantity_basis_type="qto"` means an exact, unchanged copy, not just "has some
relation to a takeoff row."** `estimates/service.py::_validate_direct_qto_quantity_copies`
re-fetches every `qto`-tagged item/component/project-cost's linked `TakeoffLineItem` and
rejects the whole proposal if the declared quantity or unit differs from that row's own
quantity/unit at all — an item that applies any conversion or factor on top of the QTO
number must be tagged `derived` (with the formula stated in its basis) instead, not `qto`.
`_validate_quantity_basis_types` also now requires a `qto`-tagged item/component to link
to **exactly one** source row (not merely "at least one"), and requires every
agent-authored **labor** component to carry a non-empty `basis` naming the operation and
quantity source, even when its quantity is `0`/`unknown` — labor can no longer go
undocumented the way it previously could.

Provenance is tracked two different ways, matching the two kinds of evidence above:
`EstimateSourceLink` ties an Item/Component back to the exact `takeoff_line_item_id` it
came from; drawing/spec evidence lives on `evidence: list[EvidenceInput]` (the same shape
`write_priced_line` uses), both on `EstimateCostComponent` (required whenever
`origin=inferred` — a validator on `EstimateComponentIn` rejects an inferred material
with no `basis`/`evidence`) and on `EstimateItem` itself. An agent-authored item satisfies
this either with a document-evidence entry, **or** with at least one QTO source link plus
a non-empty `rationale` — `_expand_source_row_mappings` rejects the whole proposal only
when an item has neither (a loosening from this rule's earlier all-items-need-evidence
form: a QTO-linked item with a stated rationale no longer strictly needs a drawing/spec
citation too). User-edited items are not evidence-checked, matching how inferred-material
evidence is already scoped. Either way the evidence's
`source_table` must be `document_nodes`, never a takeoff row id — a takeoff row is
provenance (`EstimateSourceLink`), not evidence for "where is this / what does it
require." A targeted page inspection is persisted as a non-verbatim `document_nodes`
observation and cites that stable node id.

Only after an Estimate Item and its components exist does pricing happen —
`write_estimate_component_price` fills in a component's rate. This is a second, parallel
pricing-write path alongside the pre-existing per-takeoff-line `write_priced_line` — both
independently promote into `historical_prices` today (see "Historical data source seam"
and "Open follow-ups"); that duplication is a known gap, not a designed-in feature.

The three-question derivation walk above is the reasoning freeform chat is expected to
follow when the model itself judges a message calls for it. The `categorize_estimate`
chat skill follows a considerably more elaborate, mandatory version of the same
reasoning — an explicit multi-system allocation sweep, a labor-coverage sweep, and a
bounded, agent-directed research tool rather than the three questions read literally; see
"Document research workflow" and "Estimate categorization skill" below for how that's
triggered and enforced.

## What this repo is

Backend only. A separate frontend repo owns the real UI — never scaffold product frontend
code here. This repo owns:

- The product's own REST API (FastAPI) that the frontend calls.
- The MCP server exposing tools/resources/prompts that an LLM agent uses to do the
  actual pricing work.
- All business logic and DB access.

## Architecture rules — do not deviate without asking

- **The agent never gets raw SQL or ORM access.** Every DB read/write the agent can do
  is a specific, named MCP tool with a typed schema and a tight, disambiguating
  docstring. This matters a lot: a previous version of this agent got confused about
  which tool to use, so tool descriptions must be precise and mutually exclusive —
  state what a tool is *not* for when there's a similarly-named neighbor.
- **Every priced line item gets a `source` field**: `historical_match | rfq_quote |
  agent_estimate | user_input`. This is an audit trail — don't skip it on any write
  path that prices a line item.
- **RFQs are async.** Creating one writes an editable `draft` row with selected line
  items, recipients, email copy, and vendor response links. Sending later moves the draft
  to `pending` and queues an email job, never inline in the request/response cycle. The
  FastAPI lifespan starts the background worker by default for local/single-process runs;
  deployments can disable that and run `app.workers.jobs` separately. A webhook/inbox
  handler later marks the row `fulfilled` with the quoted price. This is a real job/state
  table, not an afterthought — model retries and failure states explicitly.
- **The MCP server is mounted inside the same FastAPI app** (Streamable HTTP transport
  at `/mcp`), not run as a separate service, using the official Python MCP SDK's
  `FastMCP`. See `app/mcp/server.py` and the lifespan wiring in `app/main.py` — the
  FastMCP session manager must be started via the FastAPI app's lifespan or the mount
  will hang.
- **Business logic lives in `app/core/`.** Both the REST routes (`app/api/`) and the
  MCP tool handlers (`app/mcp/`) call into `app/core/` for pricing, matching, and RFQ
  orchestration. Never duplicate logic between the two callers — if a REST route and
  an MCP tool need the same behavior, factor it into `app/core/` and have both call it.
- **Every user-owned table's service function takes a required `user_id` and filters or
  checks it before any read/mutate.** This app is multi-tenant per-user; see
  "Authentication and multi-tenancy" below for the mechanism and the real cross-tenant
  leak this rule exists to prevent from recurring.

## Authentication and multi-tenancy

Real per-user multi-tenancy, added wholesale in a prior pass and hardened by
`3698854` ("Fix cross-tenant data leaks across projects, vendor contacts, memory, and
price book") on this branch. Flat per-user ownership — there is no company/org/tenant
entity above `User` today (`Assembly`/`AssemblyVersion` carry an unused nullable
`org_id`, see "Estimating domain model" above, but nothing else does).

- **JWT access + rotating refresh token.** `app/core/auth_jwt.py`:
  `create_access_token(user_id)` signs `{sub, iat, exp}` with `settings.
  jwt_secret_key`/`jwt_algorithm`; access tokens are stateless, short-lived
  (`jwt_access_token_ttl_seconds`), bearer-only (`fastapi.security.HTTPBearer`).
  `app/core/auth_refresh.py`: refresh tokens are opaque `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`
  strings, stored only as sha256 hashes (`refresh_tokens.token_hash`), delivered via an
  httpOnly cookie scoped to `/api/auth`. Rotation is reuse-detection: every refresh
  token belongs to a `family_id` chaining back to one login, and presenting an
  already-rotated token revokes the *whole family* — standard refresh-token-theft
  defense, not just "rotate on use."
- **Password auth** (`app/core/auth_password.py`) uses Argon2
  (`argon2.PasswordHasher`, default params). `verify_password` fails closed on both
  `VerificationError` (wrong password) and `InvalidHash` (covers a seed migration's
  placeholder hash) — a malformed hash is never allowed to raise, only to fail like a
  wrong password. `app/api/auth.py` returns one identical generic 401 for "no such
  user" and "wrong password" to prevent email enumeration; lookup is
  case-insensitive via a functional unique index on `lower(email)`.
- **`require_project_ownership`** (`app/core/auth_deps.py`) is the FastAPI dependency
  guarding essentially every project-scoped router (`agent.py`, `artifacts.py`,
  `documents.py`, `document_annotations.py`, `estimates.py`, `side_chat.py`, `jobs.py`,
  `rfqs.py`, `projects.py`, `spreadsheets.py`, `verifications.py`, and more). It depends
  on `get_current_user` (bearer token → `User` row, sets the `current_user_id`
  ContextVar), then checks `Project.id == project_id AND Project.user_id == user.id`,
  404ing identically whether the project doesn't exist or belongs to someone else — no
  IDOR-revealing 403. Its own docstring frames it as a defense-in-depth convenience
  wrapper for once Postgres RLS is fully authoritative, not the only line of defense.
- **Postgres RLS is wired in but not yet the sole enforcement mechanism.** `app/db.py`'s
  SQLAlchemy `after_begin` listener runs `select set_config('app.user_id', :user_id,
  true)` per transaction, sourced from the `current_user_id` ContextVar
  (`app/core/telemetry_context.py`). Runtime app traffic is meant to connect via
  `settings.app_database_url` — a low-privileged, non-`BYPASSRLS` role — but falls back
  to `database_url` (the table-owning role Alembic also uses) until `APP_DATABASE_URL`
  is explicitly configured, so **enabling RLS enforcement for real is a config-only
  cutover step that has not necessarily happened yet** — check which URL is actually set
  before assuming the database itself is rejecting cross-tenant rows. Two narrow,
  named escape hatches from the ContextVar-based scoping exist and are load-bearing, not
  incidental: `is_job_coordinator` (the job worker's cross-tenant claim query — a queue
  claim must see every tenant's due jobs) and `is_magic_link_lookup` (`app/api/
  rfq_responses.py`'s vendor-facing token lookup, which runs before any `current_user_id`
  exists since a vendor never logs in). `auth_deps.py` also force-commits `get_current_
  user`'s own read-only lookup to start a fresh transaction, because the session's
  connection warm-up otherwise autobegins a transaction *before* `current_user_id` is
  set, which RLS would then never see.
- **The tenancy root is `Project.user_id`**, and per its own model comment every other
  project-scoped table's `user_id` is meant to be derived from that root, not set
  independently by application code. It — and most other tables' `user_id` — is still
  **nullable**, with an explicit comment that it becomes `NOT NULL` only after a
  tenancy-backfill migration that has not run yet.
- **The `3698854` leak, as the concrete standing example of the rule above**: four
  service layers queried or mutated rows with no `user_id` filter at all — `list_
  projects` (returned every user's projects), `app/core/vendors/` (vendor-contact
  list/get/update/delete had no ownership check), `app/core/memory/service.py` (agent
  memory list/patch/forget were unfiltered, `write_memory` never set `user_id` on
  create, and two prompt-injection paths mixed every tenant's saved facts into the
  system prompt), and `app/core/price_book/` (materials/labor search and
  identity-resolution-during-import could silently match or mutate another tenant's
  existing row). The fix pattern everywhere was the same: require `user_id`, filter list
  queries by it, and check `row.user_id == user_id` before any read/mutate — returning
  not-found, not 403, on mismatch (mirroring `require_project_ownership`'s own posture).
  MCP tools get `user_id` from `require_current_user_id()` off the same `current_user_id`
  ContextVar, since they have no FastAPI dependency injection to pull it from a header.

## Admin operator console (secret-path, password-gated)

`app/api/admin.py` + `app/core/admin/service.py` (added 2026-09-02): a JSON-only
operator surface, deliberately outside JWT user auth — no User row, no bearer token.
Two gates, both required: routes exist only under `/api/admin/{ADMIN_URL_SECRET}`,
and every route requires the `X-Admin-Password` header (`require_admin`,
constant-time compare over sha256 digests). Fails closed everywhere: with either
setting unset, `app/api/__init__.py` never includes the router at all and
`require_admin` 404s as a backstop; a wrong password is also a 404 (never 401) so a
probe can't confirm the path exists; `include_in_schema=False` keeps the prefix out
of `/openapi.json`. Endpoints: `POST /users` (create account, generated-or-chosen
password, 409 on case-insensitive duplicate), `GET /users` (list), `GET
/users/{id}/activity` (summary counts + recent runs/messages/jobs/projects).
The activity read is the RLS-sensitive part: it opens a **fresh** session inside
`telemetry_context.user_id_scope(target_user_id)` — an injected `get_session()`
session would silently return zero rows, since its transaction autobegins before the
route body runs and the `after_begin` RLS hook fires once per transaction. The whole
activity report (counts, cost sum, and all four recent-item feeds) is assembled
server-side in ONE json_build_object/json_agg SQL statement (`_ACTIVITY_QUERY`) —
the original one-query-per-piece version cost ~12 sequential Neon round trips and
measured 17s wall-clock vs ~1.2s now; round trips, not row volume, were the entire
cost, so don't split it back into ORM queries. (Side effect: activity-feed
timestamps serialize as `+00:00`, not `Z`.)
`scripts/create_user.py` now delegates to the same `create_user` service function.
Never expose any of this as MCP tools. Frontend contract:
`docs/admin-console-frontend-handoff.md`. Verified live against the shared DB
(auth-layer 404s, create/duplicate/login round-trip, RLS-scoped activity returning
real per-user counts); probe rows deleted after.

## Tech stack

- Python, managed with `uv` — use `uv add`/`uv remove` for deps, never pip/poetry/conda.
- FastAPI + Uvicorn.
- MCP Python SDK (`mcp` package, `FastMCP`).
- Postgres via SQLAlchemy async + `asyncpg`, migrations via Alembic. Connection string
  comes from the `DATABASE_URL` env var (see `app/config.py`).
- Pydantic / pydantic-settings for schemas and config.
- pytest for tests, ruff for lint/format.
- `aioboto3` for Cloudflare R2 file storage (R2's S3-compatible API) — see "File storage"
  below.
- Anthropic Python SDK (`anthropic`) for the product chat agent (see "Product chat
  agent" below) and, as a mode-gated fallback, for takeoff column mapping during
  ingestion (see "Takeoff column mapping" below). OpenAI Python SDK (`openai`) is also
  wired up as a fully equivalent alternative chat agent provider (`AGENT_LLM_PROVIDER=
  openai`, `app/core/agent/openai_provider.py`), and a third value `openai-codex`
  (`app/core/agent/codex_provider.py`) runs that same OpenAI loop over a ChatGPT
  subscription transport — takeoff column mapping itself stays Claude-only regardless
  of this setting.

                LLMCall row per call (provider/model/tokens/estimated cost/a fixed
                Operation enum), keyed to telemetry_context.py's current_run_id/
                current_span_id/current_user_id ContextVars (the last of which app/db.py
                also reads for RLS — see "Authentication and multi-tenancy" above).
                telemetry_report.py builds read-only reports over persisted
                LLMCall/ToolCall/AgentRun rows, exposed via GET /api/agent/runs/{id}/
                telemetry and GET /api/projects/{id}/telemetry (the latter explicitly
                commented dev/internal-only).
    project/    Read takeoff line items and project overview/readiness aggregation (see
                below) — document retrieval itself now lives in retrieval/ and
                document_pipeline/ above, not here; this package predates that split and
                its own docstrings may still describe the older, now-retired
                get_document_outline/search_project_documents-era tools (see "Live MCP
                tool registry" above).
                summaries.py is the batched all-projects home-page read behind
                GET /api/projects/summaries (see projects.py above) — a fixed handful
                of set-based queries, deliberately serving only the fields the cards
                render; the per-project overview stays the detail read.
                overview.py aggregates scope/readiness/pricing/RFQ/quote/document counts
                into one GET /api/projects/{id}/overview payload for a project dashboard —
                read-only, composes the other app/core/* services rather than querying
                tables directly. readiness.py derives (never stores) whether active
                document uploads are still processing and whether searchable evidence
                exists — see "Project ingestion readiness" below.
    ingestion/  Direct browser-to-R2 multipart upload orchestration plus deterministic
                takeoff parsing helpers. Upload initiation records an immutable document
                and session; completion verifies object size and queues document.prepare.
                The versioned document pipeline owns extraction, structure, embeddings,
                and atomic publication. column_mapping.py holds the LLM-assisted fallback
                used when deterministic takeoff-header matching fails -- not agent-facing,
                purely an ingestion-time concern.
    pricing/    Historical-price scoring/matching, the HistoricalDataProvider seam
                (provider.py -- EstimateHistoricalProvider/RialtoHistoricalProvider/
                SyntheticHistoricalProvider, see "Historical data source seam" below),
                write_priced_line (the one function that persists a price to the
                legacy priced_line_items table + its evidence -- no longer an agent
                tool, but still called directly by the spreadsheet Apply-Pricing
                legacy branch and the priced_line_proposal verification resolver).
    estimates/  CSI-organized Estimate structure: EstimateItem (installed-work, CSI-coded)
                nesting EstimateCostComponent (material/labor/equipment/subcontract/other)

                (component pricing coverage). Independently promotes into
                historical_prices in parallel with pricing/'s write_priced_line, not yet
                reconciled -- see Open follow-ups.
    rfq/        RFQ draft creation/editing, vendor response links, send-job enqueueing, vendor lookup.
    vendor_bids/ Quote-document extraction, LLM-only quote-material grouping, persisted
                material correction/review, unit normalization, and deterministic
                takeoff-line matching. The package name remains for compatibility; its
                internal API uses quote-native names. See "Vendor quote ingestion and
