`write_estimate_component_price`, `write_project_cost`,
`search_historical_material_price`, `search_historical_labor_rate`,
`search_historical_estimate_items`, `get_estimate_pricing_status`,
`price_estimate_items`, `get_project_document_summaries`,
`list_document_understanding_cards`, `search_document_understanding`,
`research_project_documents`, `inspect_drawing_sheet`, `search_project_documents`,
`read_project_document_section`, `read_project_document_chunk`, `get_document_outline`)
no longer exist in the live registry — this section was written for a v1 tool surface
that has since been deleted, not merely superseded. It's left in place because the
design reasoning behind each retired tool's *behavior* (what counts as evidence, why
material/labor search are separate, why historical tiers are additive, etc.) mostly
still applies to whatever replaced it, but do not attempt to call any tool named below
without first checking it against the real registry list above.

The tools are organized around the four pricing `source` values, the CSI Estimate
workflow, and read-only artifact discovery/display tools, plus
read-only artifact discovery/display tools for chat artifacts and the two
user-verification-queue tools (see "User verification queue" below):

- `list_project_artifacts(project_id)` — read-only artifact discovery for the product
  chat response. It returns the currently available DB-backed Material Takeoff, Estimate,
  RFQ, Quote Comparison, and Document `AgentArtifactRef`s for a project, so the agent can
  find an existing artifact id before calling `display_artifact`. It does not read full
  artifact rows for reasoning and does not create or mutate pricing/RFQ state. A document
  only appears here once it has at least one non-superseded annotation — an uploaded file
  with nothing highlighted on it yet doesn't flood this list (see `display_artifact`'s
  `kind="document"` note below for the unrestricted, explicit-id path).
- `display_artifact(project_id, kind, rfq_id, document_id)` — read-only presentation intent
  for the product chat response. It validates that a DB-backed Material Takeoff, Estimate,
  RFQ, Quote Comparison, or Document artifact exists and returns its `AgentArtifactRef`; it
  does not read full artifact rows for reasoning and does not create or mutate pricing/RFQ
  state. **There is no separate "pricing" artifact kind** — retired along with the legacy
  per-takeoff-line pricing surface (see "Estimate artifact absorbs the legacy pricing
  artifact" below); `kind="estimate"` covers a project both before anything is priced
  (shows the unpriced CSI structure as soon as it's proposed) and after (reflects prices
  as `write_estimate_component_price`/`update_estimate_item`/the pricing batch write
  them), so there was never a state only the old pricing artifact could represent.
  `kind="document"` requires `document_id` and opens that document's review panel; unlike
  the list path above, an explicit call works even before any annotation exists.
- `highlight_document_region(project_id, document_id, node_id, page_number, quad, note)` —
  creates a highlight the user sees in the document review panel and the agent can link
  back to in chat prose (see "Identifiers in chat prose, and clickable Estimate row
  links" below for the same `workbook_ref`-style mechanism applied to documents). Prefer
  `node_id` (resolved through the same evidence path as citations, exact precision) over
  a raw `quad`; omitting both and supplying only `note` derives an approximate region via
  a fresh vision read of that page. Not for citing document text in prose — that's
  `retrieve_project_evidence`/`get_document_context`, which this tool never touches.
- `list_document_annotations(project_id, document_id)` — read-only: every highlight on
  one document, the user's and the agent's own prior ones, so the agent knows what's
  already flagged before adding another.
- `get_takeoff_line_items(project_id)` — read-only normalized takeoff scope.
- `get_estimate_structure(project_id)` — reads the active CSI-organized Estimate,
  including installed-work items, direct components, project costs, latest append-only
  prices, derived totals, and source-row coverage split into `unassigned_source_rows`
  (zero material quantity placed anywhere) and `partially_allocated_source_rows`
  (some but not all of a row's quantity placed — `remaining_quantity` says how much is
  still unaccounted for). See "Estimating domain model" above for why coverage isn't
  binary now that a material row can be split across items. If you already know which
  item ids you need, use `get_estimate_items` instead — lighter, no coverage/totals
  overhead.
- `get_estimate_items(project_id, estimate_item_ids)` — read-only, scoped to specific
  items: their info, components (materials/labor/etc. with latest prices if priced),
  and evidence, in the order requested. Raises by name on any requested id that doesn't
  belong to the project's active Estimate rather than silently dropping it. This is
  what a `price_estimate_items` subagent (below) calls to read only its assigned item.
- `begin_estimate_proposal(project_id, mode)` / `get_estimate_proposal(...)` /
  `patch_estimate_proposal(...)` / `finalize_estimate_proposal(...)` — the managed
  product-chat categorization path. It opens or resumes an internal, versioned proposal
  workspace, saves complete item replacements under stable proposal-local keys, returns
  structured validation after every patch, and exposes an Estimate artifact only after
  finalization. `mode=replace` snapshots the active Estimate without changing it;
  finalization archives the old revision and creates the new one in the same transaction.
  Managed schemas use run-local QTO/fact aliases while persistence receives authoritative
  UUID/evidence values. Drafts are internal and resumable, not user-visible artifacts.
- `propose_estimate_structure(project_id, proposal, research_dispositions)` — compatibility
  single-shot tool for external MCP clients; atomically
  writes one complete proposed Estimate revision. Direct costs must be nested under
  installed-work items; project-wide costs remain separate. Unknown source rows,
  malformed CSI values, orphan components, invalid labor inputs, a material split summing
  to more than its source row's quantity, a `qto`-tagged quantity that isn't an exact
  copy of its one linked source row, an agent-authored labor component with no `basis`,
  and an Estimate Item with neither evidence nor a QTO link plus rationale all reject the
  complete proposal — see "Estimating domain model" above for the split-quantity,
  quantity-basis, and evidence rules. `research_dispositions` is a required (possibly
  empty) list of `EstimateResearchDispositionIn` — one entry per
  `research_project_documents` question this proposal's reasoning drew on, logged as a
  tool-call audit trail only, never stored as Estimate content (see "Estimate
  categorization skill" below). Agent overwrite is blocked after estimator edits or
  approval, unless the user has just explicitly asked for a full restart — see
  `start_over_estimate` below. Not a piecemeal correction tool — use `update_estimate_item`
  to edit one existing item/component in place.
- `start_over_estimate(project_id)` — compatibility tool for external MCP clients and the
  existing REST start-over behavior. It archives the active Estimate (`status="archived"`,
  excluded from `get_active_estimate`) so the *next* `propose_estimate_structure` call
  creates a fresh `ProjectEstimate` row with `user_modified_at=None`, rather than
  hitting the same-row conflict check. This is the only way the agent can lift the
  "approved Estimates are locked" restriction below — the docstring requires the tool
  only be called when the user explicitly asks, in that exact message, to
  restart/redo/scrap the whole thing; an ambiguous request or a single wrong item
  should go through `update_estimate_item` instead, which needs no restart at all.
  Nothing is deleted (the archived draft and any prices already written under it stay
  in the database), but between this call and the next successful
  `propose_estimate_structure`, the project briefly has no active Estimate — the same
  transient state the pre-existing REST `POST .../estimate/start-over` endpoint already
  produces. Product chat never receives this tool; full rebuilds use the safe staged
  replacement workflow above. **Not yet verified against a live Postgres** — the
  create-vs-reuse logic in `save_estimate_draft` (`app/core/estimates/service.py`) was
  confirmed by reading the code (`get_active_estimate` filters out `archived` rows, so
  a fresh row gets created on the next proposal), not by running the flow against a
  real database; follow the "How this was verified" convention before trusting it in
  production.
- `update_estimate_item(project_id, estimate_item_id, updates)` — the one exception to
  "approved Estimates are locked" that needs no restart at all: corrects fields (name,
  CSI code, a component's name/quantity/basis/evidence, etc.) and/or appends a
  component price on one *existing* item in place — never creates or deletes an item,
  component, price, or source link. Every field but a component's `id` is optional and
  means "leave unchanged" when omitted; pass `""` to explicitly clear a nullable text
  field. Every call permanently marks the estimate user-modified, which then blocks
  `propose_estimate_structure`/`write_project_cost` on it until `start_over_estimate`
  runs. Not `propose_estimate_structure` (that replaces the complete structure) and not
  `write_estimate_component_price` (that only appends a price, nothing else) — use this
  specifically for "the user pointed out something wrong, fix it," not for the initial
  proposal and not for a full restart (`start_over_estimate` is for that).
- `write_estimate_component_price(project_id, component_id, price)` — appends the selected
  component price. Labor supports productivity-based pricing; all methods preserve basis,
  conditions, confidence, and evidence. Approved prices can feed historical candidates.
- `write_project_cost(project_id, project_cost)` — adds a supported project-wide cost to
  an untouched draft. It is not a back door for direct installation scope.
- `list_project_documents(project_id)`, `get_document_outline(project_id,
  project_document_id)`, `search_project_documents(project_id, query, limit)`,
  `read_project_document_section(project_id, section_pointer)`, `read_project_document_chunk(
  project_id, chunk_id)` — read-only project document context. Uploaded specs/addenda/drawings
  keep their source row in `project_documents`; extracted text is split into page/section-aware
  `project_document_chunks`, each classified with a `heading_kind` (`csi_section` |
  `csi_division` | `outline` | `None`) and, when CSI-coded, a `csi_division` — see
  `app/core/ingestion/chunking.py`. `get_document_outline` returns a document's sections as a
  navigable table of contents; each entry is a contiguous run of chunks sharing one section
  identity (a section number recurring non-contiguously — e.g. a table-of-contents mention vs.
  the real body section — is two separate entries, not merged) and carries a `section_pointer`
  (the id of that run's first chunk). `search_project_documents` is a hybrid lexical search
  (full-text + `ILIKE` + `pg_trgm` fuzzy matching for near-miss spellings, plus LLM query
  expansion grounded in the project's own section titles and takeoff label/assembly/location
  vocabulary — see `app/core/project/query_expansion.py`) rolled up to one ranked result per
  matching *section*, not per chunk; each result also carries a `section_pointer`.
  Drawing results may include separately citeable `cached_observations`, searched from
  `drawing_sheet_observations` alongside the immutable ingestion summary. Observations
  are scoped to the exact uploaded `project_document_id` and page, remain additive, and
  are omitted from search after `invalidated_at` is set.
  `read_project_document_section` reads a section's full text from that pointer, for
  understanding a requirement in context rather than as an isolated excerpt.
  `read_project_document_chunk` is the narrower fallback for a match with no `section_pointer`
  (content outside any detected section). Deliberately lexical + fuzzy, not semantic/embedding
  search — specs lean on exact codes/standards where embeddings often do worse than lexical
  matching; revisit only if a concrete retrieval failure is found, not speculatively.
- `inspect_drawing_sheet(project_id, section_pointer, question)` — performs a fresh vision
  read of one actual drawing page. The standalone tool remains read-only. The reusable
  `research_project_documents` workflow can synthesize and append a durable observation
  afterward, but only when one final atomic fact is supported by exactly one fresh drawing
  inspection; mixed spec/drawing facts, multi-sheet facts, and reused cached facts are not
  written. Cached observations can satisfy a future question without vision; if they are
  insufficient, the researcher expands and reinspects the sheet normally.
- `research_project_documents(project_id, questions)` — bounded, reusable multi-question
  document research; see "Document research workflow" above for the full plan → retrieve
  → synthesize → follow-up pipeline behind it. Takes 1-12 `DocumentResearchQuestion`
  objects in one call (each one atomic factual gap, never a combined decision) and
  returns one `resolved`/`partial`/`unresolved` finding per question with cited evidence,
  cited `conflicts`, a `stop_reason` when research stopped short of resolving the
  question (the discriminator between "the documents don't say" and "retrieval didn't
  find it" — see "Document research pipeline hardening" below), and a source inventory.
  It never makes the caller's Estimate grouping, CSI, allocation, quantity, or approval
  decision — only establishes facts for the caller to reason from.
  Internally restricted to exactly four read-only retrieval tools
  (`search_project_documents`/`read_project_document_chunk`/`read_project_document_section`/
  `inspect_drawing_sheet`); not a substitute for calling those directly outside a
  bounded research workflow, and not the same as `inspect_drawing_sheet` (which performs
  one fresh page read, no planning/synthesis, no batching).
- `get_project_document_summaries(project_id, project_document_id)`,
  `list_document_understanding_cards(project_id, project_document_id, card_kind, limit)`,
  `search_document_understanding(project_id, query, limit)` — read-only access to the
  `document.understand` job's output (per-chunk orientation cards plus a per-document
  summary, `app/core/project/understanding.py`): the cheapest first read of an ingested
  document, cheaper than paging through raw chunks via `search_project_documents`. A
  document with no summary yet (job still pending, or the role isn't in
  `_UNDERSTANDING_ROLES`) returns an empty result, not an error.
- `get_project_setup(project_id)` — reads the current versioned setup scope ledger:
  setup status/snapshot, building-system dispositions and evidence, resolved/pending
  setup questions, and explicitly defaulted assumptions. It never returns a project-fact
  or specified-material cache; retrieve those facts from source documents.
- `get_project_scope_brief(project_id)` (`app/mcp/tools/project_context.py`) — read-only
  access to the optional `ProjectScopeBrief` produced by Identify Scope. It contains the
  CSI divisions and narrative trade scope for orientation, never creates Estimate
  content, and is not itself citable Estimate evidence. Categorization proceeds directly
  from project evidence and the QTO when no current brief exists.
- `search_historical_material_price(project_id, label, unit)`,
  `search_historical_labor_rate(project_id, label, unit)`
  — historical lookups, kept as **separate tools** (not one combined tool) because material
  and labor follow genuinely different fallback paths per the product flow. Each merges
  candidates from up to three tiers (see "Historical data source seam" below) and returns
  a `HistoricalPriceSearchResult`: `candidates` (top-10 ranked, with a compatibility score
  and rejection reasons — `unit_mismatch`, `weak_label_match`, `missing_price`) plus
  `stats` (`count`/`mean`/`median`/`mode`/`min`/`max`/`quartiles`) computed over the
  **full accepted pool**, which may be larger than the 10 shown — use `stats` to judge
  the typical price range even without inspecting every candidate. An empty/all-rejected
  result means "fall back to RFQ," not "price is zero." Every candidate carries a
  `source_table` field saying which tier it came from (`estimate_cost_components` |
  `historical_prices` | `synthetic_estimate_lines`) — cite that alongside the candidate's
  `id` as evidence when calling `write_estimate_component_price`. Scoring lives in
  `app/core/pricing/scoring.py` (token overlap + unit-alias compatibility), written
  fresh — see "Reference repo" below for why; scoring itself doesn't weight by tier,
  that's left to the agent's judgment.
- `search_historical_estimate_items(csi_code, label)` — company-wide (no `project_id`,
  same posture as `historical_prices`), finds previously-priced Estimate Items from
  **other** projects under the same CSI code, optionally narrowed by wording overlap.
  Returns full item context (evidence, components with latest prices), not a flat price
  number, so the agent can judge applicability the way it judges `historical_match` vs
  `agent_estimate` elsewhere. Deliberately a **separate, heavier, on-demand** tool
  rather than a fourth tier merged into the two search tools above — same precedent as
  `inspect_drawing_sheet` being separate from the cheap always-on
  `search_project_documents`.
- `get_estimate_pricing_status(project_id)` — read-only: which of the active Estimate's
  components already have a price and which don't. A component absent from the result
  hasn't been priced yet — same "absence is the signal, no stored flag" philosophy the
  now-retired `get_pricing_status` used for takeoff lines. Cross-reference against
  `get_estimate_structure`/`get_estimate_items` for full scope vs. what's missing.

**Retired as agent tools**: `write_priced_line` and `get_pricing_status` (the
per-takeoff-line, pre-Estimate `priced_line_items` tools) are no longer registered —
every project now builds an Estimate, and pricing happens through
`write_estimate_component_price`/`get_estimate_pricing_status` instead. This is an MCP
boundary change only: the underlying `app.core.pricing.service.write_priced_line`
function and the `priced_line_items` table are untouched, since
`app/core/spreadsheets/service.py`'s legacy Apply-Pricing branch and the
`priced_line_proposal` verification resolver both still call it directly (never through
MCP). A pre-Estimate project's chat pricing is now **queue-only**: the system prompt's
fallback flow always routes through `request_user_verification(kind=
priced_line_proposal)` rather than writing directly — see "Product chat agent" below.
- `list_vendor_contacts(trade, material)`, `create_rfq(project_id, line_item_ids,
  vendor_ids)`, `send_rfq(rfq_id)`, `get_rfq_status(rfq_id)` — RFQ tools. `create_rfq`
  writes an editable `draft` RFQ and selected line/vendor rows; `send_rfq` transitions that
  draft to `pending` and writes the `rfq.send` `Job` row. Neither sends email inline. The
  **automatic** inbound quote handler — the one that would mark an RFQ `fulfilled` and
  write a `source=rfq_quote` price the moment a vendor's reply lands — is
  **not yet implemented** — model exists (`quote_submissions`), handler doesn't. A
  **manual** path to the same `source=rfq_quote` write exists today via the quote
  comparison spreadsheet's apply-pricing action (see "Quote comparison spreadsheet"
  below); that's an estimator picking among already-submitted quotes, not the inbound
  webhook itself.
- `get_quote_comparison(project_id)` — read-only: compares vendor `quote_submissions`
  from RFQ responses and direct document imports. Takeoff projects render matched quote
  lines; no-takeoff projects render persisted quote-material groups. Does not create an
  RFQ, send email, or ingest a vendor reply. Delegates to the same spreadsheet builder the
  `/api/projects/{id}/spreadsheets/quote-comparison/state` REST endpoint uses (see "Quote
  comparison spreadsheet" below), so its return shape is the full `SpreadsheetWorkbook`
  (per-cell formatting/overlay/protection metadata) built for the estimator grid UI, not a
  lean agent-specific projection — heavier than the other read tools here, worth trimming
  if it turns out to add noticeable noise to the agent's context.
- `list_vendor_quote_line_items(project_id)` — reads every
  `VendorQuoteLineItem` extracted from uploaded quote documents, matched and unmatched.
- `create_takeoff_line_item_from_vendor_quote(vendor_quote_line_item_id)` — the only tool
  that writes `takeoff_line_items` outside of CSV/XLSX ingestion. Its legacy MCP name
  promotes one unmatched quote line into a new takeoff line item.
  Raises if the line is already matched, or if it's missing quantity/unit (never
  fabricates placeholder values).

- `request_user_verification(project_id, kind, reason, payload, confidence)` — queues a
  low-confidence proposal for the user's explicit review instead of writing it. Only two
  `agent_raisable` kinds are allowed: `priced_line_proposal` (legacy, pre-Estimate
  projects — resolver routes through `write_priced_line` with `source=user_input`) and
  `estimate_component_price_proposal` (Estimate-domain — resolver routes through
  `write_estimate_component_price`). Use whichever matches the project's state; raising
  `priced_line_proposal` for an Estimate component targets the wrong table. Raising
  again for the same subject supersedes the earlier pending request. Not a direct write
  tool — the docstrings state this both ways.
- `list_pending_verifications(project_id)` — read-only view of the project's pending
  verification queue (all kinds, not just agent-raised ones), so the agent can report
  what's awaiting the user's review. Resolution itself is user-only, via REST.
- `price_estimate_items(project_id, estimate_item_ids)` — queues a background pass
  (`estimate.price_batch` job) that prices the given Estimate Items: one independent
  subagent per item, run concurrently across items (bounded by
  `settings.estimate_pricing_concurrency`), each pricing its own components one at a
  time. Validates the ids up front and returns a job id immediately — it does not price
  inline and does not return prices; check `get_estimate_pricing_status`/
  `get_estimate_items` afterward. The one entry point for both a hand-picked subset
  (infer ids from what the user asked for) and, later, a whole-project trigger — see
  "Parallel pricing execution" below.

There's also a `ping` tool (proves the `/mcp` mount works, nothing to do with pricing).
`app/core/agent/tools.py` excludes it when building the tool list for the chat agent so
it doesn't add noise to what the LLM has to reason about — external MCP clients (Claude
Code, Claude Desktop) still see it.

## Estimate artifact absorbs the legacy pricing artifact

The `"pricing"` `ArtifactKind` (backed by `PricedLineItem`, the pre-Estimate
per-takeoff-line world) is fully retired, not just deprioritized — `app/core/
artifacts/types.py`'s `ArtifactKind` no longer includes it, and `PricingArtifact`/
`PricingArtifactRow` are deleted. This follows the `write_priced_line`/
`get_pricing_status` MCP retirement (see "MCP tool catalog" above): since every project
is Estimate-based now, the Estimate artifact (`kind="estimate"`) already covers both
halves of what the pricing artifact used to show on its own — the unpriced structure
right after `propose_estimate_structure`/`categorize_estimate`, and the priced one once
`write_estimate_component_price`/`update_estimate_item`/the pricing batch fill it in —
so keeping a second artifact for the "priced" half was redundant, not complementary.

- **Removed**: `get_pricing_artifact` (`app/core/artifacts/service.py`), `pricing_ref`
  (its discovery/display-existence helper), the `GET /api/projects/{id}/artifacts/
  pricing` REST route, the `kind == "pricing"` branch in `display_artifact_ref`, and the
  `_refs_for_tool_call` auto-attach branch keyed on `{"get_pricing_status",
  "write_priced_line"}` — that branch was already dead code (those tool names haven't
  been in the MCP registry since the prior pass) before this cleanup removed it outright.
  `PricedLineItem`/`write_priced_line` themselves are untouched — they still back the
  legacy spreadsheet Apply-Pricing branch and the `priced_line_proposal` verification
  resolver for a pre-Estimate project (see "MCP tool catalog"'s retirement note); only
  the *artifact* (display/discovery layer) is gone, not the underlying write path.
- **`GET /overview`'s `pricing` section is now Estimate-based, not `PricedLineItem`-based.**
  `ProjectOverviewArtifacts.pricing` field is removed (there's no artifact ref for it
  anymore); `ProjectOverviewPricing` (the `pricing` field on the overview payload) keeps
  its existing shape (`priced_count`/`unpriced_count`/`extended_total`/`source_counts`/
  `last_priced_at`) but is now built by `estimates/service.py::get_estimate_pricing_summary`
  over `EstimateCostComponent`/`EstimateComponentPrice` (all components of the active
  Estimate, direct and project-wide, outer-joined to each one's latest price) instead of
  `PricedLineItem`. Unlike `get_estimate_pricing_status` (the MCP tool, which lists only
  priced components and raises if there's no active Estimate — correct for an agent that
  already confirmed one exists), `get_estimate_pricing_summary` counts unpriced
  components too and returns an all-zero summary rather than raising when a project
  hasn't been categorized into an Estimate yet, since a dashboard must render that state,
  not error on it.
- **`ProjectOverviewScope.assemblies[].priced_count` is also Estimate-based now**, via
  `app/core/project/overview.py::_priced_takeoff_line_item_ids` — a takeoff row counts as
  priced if it has a component-level `EstimateSourceLink` (a `row_type=material` mapping,
  see "Estimating domain model") into a component that currently has a price.
  Deliberately does **not** resolve item-level links (`installed_work`/`allowance`
  mappings) transitively through an item's components: an item-level link traces "this
  row seeded this item existing," not "this row's own material is priced," and the two
  are kept semantically distinct everywhere else in the domain model (see "Estimating
  domain model"'s provenance section) — conflating them here would be a new, undocumented
  exception to that rule, not a faithful port of the old per-line-item "is this priced"
  signal. This logic lives directly in `overview.py` rather than `estimates/service.py`,
  matching this file's existing pattern of querying `TakeoffLineItem`/`Rfq`/
  `QuoteSubmission` directly for dashboard-only aggregations — assembly grouping is a
  takeoff/overview concept, not an Estimate one (Estimate Items are never grouped by
  assembly; see "Estimating domain model").
- **Not verified against a live Postgres this pass** — same limitation as the rest of
  this session's work (no local Postgres credentials available); the two new queries
  (`get_estimate_pricing_summary`'s outer-join-to-latest-price subquery and
  `_priced_takeoff_line_item_ids`'s source-link join) were confirmed to compile to valid
  SQL against the real model definitions (`Compile()`), and `ruff`/`pytest`/a full
  `app.main` import all pass, but the actual aggregate numbers have not been checked
  against seeded rows in a real database. Run that pass, per the "How this was verified"
  convention, before trusting `GET /overview`'s `pricing`/`scope.assemblies[].priced_count`
  fields in production.

## Product chat agent (manual bridging loop)

`POST /api/projects/{project_id}/agent/messages` is a real product-chat surface — the
backend itself acts as the MCP *host*, not just the tool server. There's no external app
(Claude Code, Claude Desktop) doing the host job here. This section describes the main
project chat surface specifically — see "Agent run streaming and the three chat
surfaces" below for how it relates to `side_chat` and `user_wide_agent`, and for the
`start_message_run`/`complete_message_run` split that now sits in front of the
`handle_message` entrypoint described below (kept as a thin synchronous wrapper over
both, for callers that don't need to stream).

- **One tool registry, two consumption paths.** `app/core/agent/tools.py` calls
  `mcp.list_tools()` / `mcp.call_tool()` **in-process** on the same `FastMCP` instance
  Claude Code talks to over HTTP at `/mcp`. Tool schemas and behavior can never drift
  between "external MCP client" and "product chat" because there's only one definition.
- **Provider seam, not a single hardcoded call.** `app/core/agent/provider.py` defines
  `LLMProvider.run_agentic_turn(system, conversation) -> AgentTurnResult`. A provider owns the
  *entire* multi-turn tool-calling loop for one message, not just one HTTP request —
  Claude's content-block format and OpenAI's tool-calls format differ enough that
  leaking either into the orchestrator would defeat the seam. Two equivalent
  implementations exist: `ClaudeProvider` (`app/core/agent/claude_provider.py`, uses
  Claude's Messages API) and `OpenAIProvider` (`app/core/agent/openai_provider.py`, uses
  OpenAI's Responses API — the only OpenAI API surface that supports both custom tools
  and a hosted web search tool in one call). A third value selects
  `CodexSubscriptionProvider` — see the subscription-transport bullet below.
  `AGENT_LLM_PROVIDER=claude|openai|openai-codex` selects between them (default
  `claude`); the selection lives in `app/core/agent/factory.py`'s `get_llm_provider`,
  not in `provider.py` itself, since that module is deliberately implementation-free and
  every provider already imports from it — a factory there importing them back would be
  circular. (`orchestrator.py` still has a `_get_llm_provider`, but it is now a two-line
  delegate to `factory.get_llm_provider`, not the place the choice is actually made.)
  Both API-key providers bridge the same MCP tool
  registry, run a bounded multi-turn loop (`MAX_TOOL_TURNS = 12`,
  `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 8192` in each), declare a server-side web search tool
  (`web_search_20260209` for Claude, `web_search` for OpenAI) that's resolved entirely
  server-side within one API call, and treat a token-limit truncation the same way:
  run whatever tool calls did come through complete, then nudge the model to continue
  rather than discarding the turn's progress (Claude: `stop_reason == "max_tokens"`;
  OpenAI: `response.status == "incomplete"`). `run_agentic_turn` also takes an
  `allowed_tool_names: frozenset[str] | None` (a strict allow-list, applied before
  `excluded_tool_names`) and `include_server_tools: bool` (set `False` to hide the
  hosted web search tool from a bounded internal workflow) — see "Estimate
  categorization skill" below for where both are used.
- **`AGENT_LLM_PROVIDER=openai-codex` is a third provider: the same OpenAI agent loop
  run over a ChatGPT subscription instead of an API key.**
  `CodexSubscriptionProvider` (`app/core/agent/codex_provider.py`) **subclasses**
  `OpenAIProvider` rather than reimplementing it — it inherits the whole multi-turn
  tool-calling loop and overrides only what the subscription transport needs:
  `__init__` (holds a placeholder `AsyncOpenAI` the parent uses for capability
  detection only; every real request gets a freshly refreshed subscription-authenticated
  client), `_create_response`, `_stream_agentic_response`, and `run_structured_turn`.
  The recurring reason for the last two is the same: **the ChatGPT subscription
  Responses transport rejects `max_output_tokens` outright**, so
  `_stream_agentic_response` pops it out of the kwargs the parent loop supplied and
  `run_structured_turn` deletes its own copy, keeping the parameter in the signature
  for provider parity while letting the subscription endpoint apply its own output
  bound. Both request paths also force `store=False` and
  `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`. Auth comes from
  `codex_auth.get_access_credentials` (account id + access token, sent as
  `ChatGPT-Account-ID` plus originator/version/session headers against
  `openai_codex_base_url`, default `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`), and a
  rate/usage cap raises `CodexQuotaError` — there is deliberately **no API-billing
  fallback**. `app/config.py` gates it: `agent_llm_provider` is a
  `Literal["claude", "openai", "openai-codex"]`, `resolved_openai_codex_model` falls
  back to `openai_model` when `openai_codex_model` is blank, and a non-development
  `openai-codex` run without `openai_codex_token_encryption_secret` fails startup.
  The same transport also serves ingestion-side vision (`run_codex_pdf_prompt`/
  `run_codex_image_prompt`).
- **A second, schema-constrained call shape exists alongside the tool-calling loop.**
  `LLMProvider.run_structured_turn[T: BaseModel](system, conversation, output_type,
  max_output_tokens, reasoning_effort) -> T` returns one tool-free, schema-validated
  response — for internal reducers that need reliable structured output without the
  overhead/nondeterminism of a full tool-calling turn, not for anything the chat host
  itself calls directly. Both `ClaudeProvider`/`OpenAIProvider` implement it by mapping
  `output_type` to their native structured-output API (Claude:
  `messages.parse(output_format=...)`). Its first (and so far only) caller is the
  "Document research workflow" above's planning/synthesis steps.
- **The orchestrator sees a provider-neutral final answer shape.** `app/core/agent/orchestrator.py`
  (`handle_message`) loads a project's `AgentMessage` history as plain
  `SimpleMessage(role, content)` pairs, hands them to the provider, and persists the
  final prose plus ordered `content_blocks` for UI placement. The tool_use/tool_result
  exchange within a turn is never persisted to chat history, matching the "chat history
  is continuity, not audit trail" rule.
- **`current_run_id` ContextVar threads the audit trail through, without touching the
  public tool schema.** Each call to `handle_message` creates one `AgentRun` row (one
  per chat message, covering however many tool calls that message took), sets
  `current_run_id` for the duration of the provider's loop, and every `run_logged_tool`
  call picks it up automatically as its `tool_calls.run_id` if the caller didn't pass one
  explicitly. External MCP clients never set this ContextVar, so their tool calls still
  get `run_id = NULL` exactly as before — this is additive, not a behavior change for
  Claude Code.
- **Separation between projects is structural, not special-cased.** Every query is
  scoped by `project_id`; two projects' conversations, runs, and tool calls never share
  any in-memory state, only the underlying `historical_prices`/`vendor_contacts` tables
  (which are intentionally company-wide, not project-scoped — see the cross-project
  historical-match test in "How this was verified").
- **Guardrails and the pricing-flow policy live in the system prompt**
  (`SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` in `orchestrator.py`), not in the tools — refusal of
  off-domain questions, the historical→estimate/RFQ/user-input fallback order, and
  "always write or queue a price, never just say a number in chat" are all prompt-level
  rules the orchestrator doesn't enforce in code. If those need to be hard guarantees
  rather than LLM-followed conventions, that's future work. **One exception**: a skill
  turn's tool exclusions (`app.core.agent.skills`, see "Estimate categorization skill" below)
  are a real code-level guarantee, not a prompt convention — `run_agentic_turn`'s
  `excluded_tool_names` param removes the excluded tools from what the provider even
  sends the model, so `categorize_estimate` is structurally incapable of calling a
  pricing-write tool regardless of what the model decides to do.

## Identifiers in chat prose, and clickable Estimate row links

Two halves of one problem on the "Ask about this estimate" surface: raw UUIDs were
reaching the user's screen, and there was no way for the agent to point at an Estimate
row except by printing its id.

**The leak, and why it happened.** A real reply (project "Test Project",
`agent_messages.id=1b7135c3-…`) opened "I chose the selected components because they are
the QTO rows…" and then listed six components by raw UUID. Confirmed against the DB, not
inferred: those six are exactly the `logical_key`s of the six `workbook_annotation`
blocks on the preceding user message (`0fd26ec1-…`), in order — the user had selected an
item plus six component cells. They are not takeoff rows at all (none of the ids exist in
`takeoff_line_items`); the model's own "QTO rows" wording was wrong too.
`_with_annotation_context` (`orchestrator.py`) rendered each selection as
`component "<name>" (logical_key: <uuid>)` and then instructed the model to "address each
selection directly, using its logical_key with get_estimate_draft/patch_estimate_draft."
Both named tools are dead ends here — `patch_estimate_draft` is excluded from plain chat,
and `get_estimate_draft`'s `ItemOut`/`ComponentOut` expose no logical key at all — so
there was no way to *use* the id except to repeat it, and no rule anywhere forbidding
that.

- **The key still gets passed** — `set_component_price` consumes exactly this value, and
  the links below need it. What changed is that it is labelled machine-only, the
  instruction now names `set_component_price` (the one tool that actually takes it), and
  the model is told to refer to each selection by its quoted name.
- **`csi_node_id` is now in `_CONTEXT_EXCLUDED_FIELDS`** (`chat_annotations.py`). It is a
  top-level scalar on `InstalledWorkItemDraft`, so it landed in `snapshot_values`
  automatically and was a second raw UUID in the same prompt text, with no agent-facing
  use — the CSI code/title it stands for already arrive via `get_estimate_draft`.
- **An "Identifier policy" section in `CONTENT_BLOCKS_FORMAT_INSTRUCTIONS`**
  (`app/core/agent/content.py`) generalizes the rule, because the annotation suffix was
  not the only leak: `get_takeoff_line_items.id`, `QtoRowCoverageOut.takeoff_line_item_id`,
  and `ComponentPricingOut.component_id` are all reachable in freeform and all previously
  undocumented for prose. That section is appended to *every* turn, so the rule covers
  skills too. It also promotes the `R<n>`/`C<n>` display aliases to a prompt-level
  convention — until now `ComponentPricingOut.component_ref`'s field docstring ("for
  prose/questions") was the only place that convention existed anywhere.

**`workbook_ref`, the inverse of a workbook annotation.** An annotation is the user
pointing at a cell; a `workbook_ref` is the assistant pointing back. It is a fourth
`AgentResponseBlock` (alongside text/artifact/citation) and a new `ChatContentBlock`,
carrying `anchor_text` + `target_kind` + `logical_key`, enriched server-side with `label`
and `artifact_id`. `anchor_text` is a verbatim substring of the message's own prose (the
material name as written) that the frontend wraps in a link; there is deliberately **no
visible marker** like a citation's `[N]`, since the entire point is that the reader sees
a name and never an id. `logical_key` equals `EstimateItemOut.id`/`EstimateComponentOut.id`
in the Estimate artifact payload verbatim (both are `str(logical_*_key)`), so a click
resolves a row by direct id equality with no extra request — which is why the click
target is the existing `kind="estimate"` artifact rather than the workbook grid (the
workbook is REST-only and not a registered `ArtifactKind`).

- **Validation is post-turn, modeled on `_enrich_citations`.**
  `orchestrator._resolve_workbook_refs` drops any reference whose `logical_key` isn't a
  row of the project's current draft, whose `anchor_text` doesn't occur in the message's
  own prose, or that duplicates a row already linked. **Dropping, not keeping, is the
  deliberate difference from citations**: an unresolvable citation is kept because the
  frontend can retry it through the evidence resolve endpoint, whereas a stale row id has
  no retry path — and dropping is lossless here, since the anchor text is already
  ordinary prose and simply renders unlinked.
- **`lookup_workbook_row_labels`** (`chat_annotations.py`) is the read-only, non-raising
  counterpart to `resolve_workbook_annotations`, sharing one `_draft_row_lookups` helper
  rather than duplicating graph loading in the orchestrator. The two differ on purpose:
  an unknown key from a *user* click is a bad request, while an unknown key from the
  *model* just means the reference gets dropped.
- **Scope limit**: the agent can only link a row it was handed the key for — a selected
  cell, or a component from `get_estimate_pricing_state`. Since `get_estimate_draft`
  returns no logical keys, a reply naming a component nobody selected generally cannot
  link it and writes the name unlinked. Adding keys to that read shape is the follow-up
  if it matters.
- **Additive and frontend-gated.** No migration (`content_blocks` is JSON), no changed
  field, no changed endpoint; an unrendering frontend just shows plain text. The
  rendering contract is `docs/chat-workbook-refs-frontend-handoff.md`, following the
  `docs/price-book-frontend-handoff.md` precedent.
- **Not verified**: no live LLM run has emitted a `workbook_ref` yet — the block,
  validation, and prompt layers are unit-tested (`tests/test_agent_runs.py`,
  `tests/test_chat_annotations.py`), but whether the model reliably emits one with a
  correctly copied `anchor_text`, and whether the prompt changes actually stop the UUID
  echo under a real model, both need a live pass. The exact reproducing input is still in
  the DB (user message `0fd26ec1-…` and its seven annotation blocks) — replay that turn
  and assert no UUID appears in the persisted `body`/`content_blocks`. This environment
  is `AGENT_LLM_PROVIDER=openai`; the Claude path is unverified, as everywhere else here.

## Estimate categorization skill

`categorize_estimate` is the first (and so far only) entry in `app.core.agent.skills`'s
`SKILL_DIRECTIVES`/`SKILL_ALLOWED_TOOLS` — a fixed, mandatory procedure the estimator
triggers explicitly, distinct from the freeform "Estimate workflow" prose in
`SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` that only runs when the model itself judges a message calls for
it. Freeform chat's own "Estimate workflow" prose still reasons tool-by-tool over
`inspect_drawing_sheet`/`search_project_documents` directly and is never routed through
`research_project_documents`; only this skill's dedicated procedure is.

- **Trigger is a structured field, not text parsing.** `POST .../agent/messages`
  (`SendMessageRequest.skill: Literal["categorize_estimate"] | None`) — the frontend
  renders the "/" affordance and sets this explicitly, the same way `mentioned_document_ids`
  is already a structured field rather than something parsed out of the raw message body.
  `handle_message(..., skill=...)` threads it through.
- **This skill gets an entirely separate system prompt, not just an appended directive.**
  `orchestrator.py::_build_system_prompt` swaps in `CATEGORIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE`
  (its own restatement of the Estimate invariants, tuned for this skill) instead of the
  ordinary `SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` when `skill == "categorize_estimate"`, then still
  appends `SKILL_DIRECTIVES["categorize_estimate"]` and
  `ESTIMATE_RESEARCH_ADMISSION_RULES` (`app.core.agent.skills`) on top. The directive
  itself no longer reads as a literal three-question walk — it's a multi-step audit: form
  a provisional structure from the QTO, run an explicit multi-system material-allocation
  sweep and a labor-coverage sweep across every provisional item, convert only genuinely
  consequential gaps into atomic questions for `research_project_documents` (submitted as
  one batched call — see "Document research workflow" above), then map rows and propose.
  The admission rules exist specifically to stop the skill from either over-researching
  (asking about everything) or under-researching (guessing past a real gap) — research
  only a decision with a credible competing interpretation, never for reassurance.
  `include_server_tools=False` for this skill turn — web search is unavailable, keeping
  categorization grounded only in this project's own documents and QTO.
- **Tool restriction is now a hard allow-list, not an exclude-list.** The
  `LLMProvider.run_agentic_turn` ABC (`app/core/agent/provider.py`) takes both an
  `excluded_tool_names: frozenset[str]` and a newer `allowed_tool_names: frozenset[str] |
  None` param, both threaded into `list_tool_definitions()`/`execute_tool()`
  (`app/core/agent/tools.py`) — a call naming a disallowed tool is hard-rejected before it
  reaches `app.mcp.server.mcp`, not merely discouraged. **Stale below, corrected in
  "Stage 2-4"**: `SKILL_ALLOWED_TOOLS["categorize_estimate"]` as described in this
  paragraph (`{get_takeoff_line_items, research_project_documents,
  get_estimate_proposal, patch_estimate_proposal, finalize_estimate_proposal}`) was the
  v1 optimized-mode set; the Stage 2-4 rewrite replaced it with a 12-tool set that
  includes `get_project_scope_brief`/`get_project_document_summaries`/
  `search_document_understanding`/`list_document_understanding_cards`/
  `get_document_outline`/`search_project_documents`/`read_project_document_section`/
  `inspect_drawing_sheet` alongside `research_project_documents` and the three
  `get`/`patch`/`finalize_estimate_draft` v2 tools — see "Stage 2-4"'s own "New MCP
  tools" subsection for the current, accurate list. The direct document-read tools were
  never removed for this skill; what changed in the research-pipeline pass below is only
  that they're the escalation path (a `stop_reason` retrieval gap, a returned conflict,
  a verbatim schedule cell a synthesized claim flattened, a gap a rejected patch
  exposed), not the default one — a single batched `research_project_documents` call is.
  The real, still-accurate guarantee this hard allow-list gives: no pricing-write tool
  is reachable from this skill regardless of which document tools are.
- **Managed categorization is resumable and terminal only on finalization.** The
  orchestrator opens or resumes an `EstimateProposal`, preloads its QTO aliases and
  persisted research facts, and requires explicit allocation/exclusion/unresolved
  coverage for every row. Patches replace only named item keys. A successful
  `finalize_estimate_proposal` is terminal and deterministically displays the committed
  artifact; provider failure leaves the draft and active Estimate intact.
- **No more fixed 40-tool-turn override.** `SKILL_MAX_TOOL_TURNS["categorize_estimate"]`
  was removed (the dict is empty), reverting this skill to each provider's default budget
  of 12 — the old override existed because the now-deleted `categorize_batch.py`
  pre-investigation pass made every categorization turn long-running by construction; the
  batched research tool is expected to need far fewer round-trips, though this hasn't been
  load-tested against a large, ambiguity-heavy real project (see "Document research
  workflow"'s unhandled >12-question overflow case above).
- **`propose_estimate_structure` requires a `research_dispositions` argument on every
  call, not only from this skill.** One `EstimateResearchDispositionIn` (`question_id`,
  `action` — `applied_facts`/`decision_left_unresolved`/`no_decision_change` —,
  `rationale`) per question the proposal's reasoning actually drew on, or `[]` when no
  research was needed; it's a tool-call audit trail only, never persisted as Estimate
  content, and is only logged into `tool_calls.arguments`, not stored on the Estimate
  itself.
- **No new `AgentRun` field for skill attribution** — deliberately, to avoid a second
  migration alongside `EstimateItem.evidence` (see "Database state" below). If skill
  attribution is needed later, prefix `AgentRun.goal` instead of adding a column.

## Skill auto-detection

A skill's stricter procedure previously only ran when the frontend's "/" picker set
`SendMessageRequest.skill` explicitly — a user who typed the same intent in ordinary
chat ("build out the estimate structure," "go ahead and price the rest of the
estimate") got freeform chat instead, missing the research-driven categorization rigor
or the whole-Estimate pricing queue entirely. `app/core/agent/skill_router.py` closes
this gap with a small, bounded classifier, not text/keyword parsing — it reuses the
same `LLMProvider.run_structured_turn` seam "Document research workflow" built for
schema-constrained, tool-free reasoning.

- **Whitelisted and conservative.** `SKILL_AUTO_INVOCABLE = {"categorize_estimate",
  "price_estimate"}` gates which skills this mechanism may ever select — extensible
  for future skills, not automatic for every entry in `SkillName`. `detect_skill`
  (called from `orchestrator.handle_message`, only when the caller left `skill=None`
  and `settings.agent_skill_auto_detection_enabled` is true) sends the last
  `SKILL_DETECTION_HISTORY_LIMIT` (6) conversation messages to one `run_structured_turn`
  call against `SkillDetection` (`skill`, `confidence: low|medium|high`, `rationale`).
  Only a `"high"`-confidence, non-null result (checked by
  `orchestrator._resolve_effective_skill`, not inside `detect_skill` itself) ever
  overrides freeform chat — `"low"`/`"medium"`/`skill=None` all mean "proceed as
  ordinary chat," matching the deliberately cautious posture of not guessing past real
  ambiguity that already governs `categorize_estimate`'s own research admission rules.
- **`price_estimate` has a narrower trigger than `categorize_estimate`.**
  `SKILL_TRIGGER_GUIDANCE["price_estimate"]` explicitly instructs the classifier to
  match only a request to price the *entire* remaining Estimate ("price everything,"
  "price out what's left") — never a request naming one material, labor activity, CSI
  code, or a named subset ("price the drywall labor," "price these 3 items"). That
  narrower case must fall through to ordinary freeform chat, which already calls
  `price_estimate_items` directly with just the relevant ids — auto-invoking the
  `price_estimate` *skill* for a subset request would be wrong, since that skill's
  directive always queues every unpriced item in the whole active Estimate, regardless
  of what the user actually asked for.
- **Fails closed, same convention as the takeoff-column-mapping LLM fallback.** Any
  exception in `detect_skill` (timeout, malformed structured output, provider error) is
  caught and treated as "no match," mirroring
  `app.core.ingestion.column_mapping.maybe_map_columns_with_llm`'s existing
  LLM-failure-returns-`None` pattern — a classifier hiccup must never break or block an
  ordinary chat turn. `agent_skill_auto_detection_enabled` (`app/config.py`, default
  `True`) is a plain kill switch if it needs disabling without a code change.
- **Never overrides an explicit choice, and is visible when it fires.**
  `_resolve_effective_skill` only ever fills in a skill the caller left unset; it can
  never override `SendMessageRequest.skill`. When it does apply, `_build_system_prompt`
  appends one extra instruction telling the model to open its reply with a short, plain
  sentence stating it's treating the message as a `categorize_estimate`/`price_estimate`
  request — so a user isn't confused by a turn that behaves differently (no web search,
  a restricted tool set) than an ordinary chat reply would. The turn is also tagged for
  audit purposes: `AgentRun.goal` is prefixed with `f"auto_skill:{skill}:"`, the same
  no-migration-needed convention already used for
  `"estimate.price_batch:{job_id}:item:{item_id}"`.
- **Not verified against a live LLM this pass** — same limitation as the rest of this
  repo's LLM-tool-choice-dependent work (see "How this was verified"): fake-provider
  unit tests (`tests/test_skill_router.py`, `tests/test_orchestrator_skill_routing.py`)
  confirm the confidence-threshold/fail-closed/never-override-explicit-choice logic and
  the transparency-instruction wiring, but whether the classifier prompt actually
  distinguishes "price everything" from "price this one item" reliably in practice
  needs a manual pass against a real project before trusting it in production.
